title.raw: 卷四十 志第三十 百官下 Volume 40 Treatises 30: Officials 2

sentences.zh: 志第三十 百官下

translations.literal: Treatise 30: Officials (Part 2).
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 30 — Lower Officials.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎，四人，與侍中俱掌門下眾事。

translations.literal: Supervisors of Attendants at the Yellow Gate, four persons; together with the Palace Attendants they managed all affairs of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Supervisors of Attendants at the Yellow Gates; together with the Palace Attendants they oversaw all Chancellery affairs.

sentences.zh: 郊廟臨軒，則一人執麾。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifices and temple ceremonies when facing the hall, one person held the banner.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban rites and temple ceremonies when the emperor sat facing the hall, one of them held the ceremonial banner.

sentences.zh: 《漢百官表》秦曰給事黃門，無員，掌侍從左右，漢因之。

translations.literal: The Han Tables of Officials states that under Qin the title was Attendant Serving at the Yellow Gate, with no fixed quota, in charge of attending left and right; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Han Tables of Officials, under the Qin the office was called Attendant Serving at the Yellow Gate, without a fixed quota, attending at the ruler's left and right; the Han adopted the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 漢東京曰給事黃門侍郎，亦無員，掌侍從左右，關通中外，諸王朝見，則引王就坐。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital called them Supervisors of Attendants at the Yellow Gate, also without fixed quota, attending left and right, connecting inside and outside; when feudal kings had audience, they led the king to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the title was Supervisor of Attendants at the Yellow Gate, again without a fixed quota, attending at left and right and linking the inner and outer courts; when feudal kings came for audience, they escorted the king to his seat.

sentences.zh: 應劭曰：「每日莫向青瑣門拜，謂之夕郎。」

translations.literal: Ying Shao says: "Every evening they bow toward the Green Lattice Gate, and are called Evening Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao writes: "Each evening they bow toward the Green Lattice Gate, whence they are called Evening Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 史臣按，劉向與子歆書曰：「黃門郎，顯處也。」

translations.literal: The historian comments: In Liu Xiang's letter to his son Xin it says: "Yellow Gate Attendant is a prominent post."
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: in Liu Xiang's letter to his son Xin he writes, "Yellow Gate Attendant is a conspicuous post."

sentences.zh: 然則前漢世已為黃門侍郎矣。

translations.literal: Thus in the Former Han era it was already Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even in the Former Han the post was already called Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 董巴《漢書》曰：「禁門曰黃闥，中人主之，故號曰黃門令。」

translations.literal: Dong Ba's Han shu says: "The forbidden gate is called the Yellow Portal; eunuchs preside over it, hence the title Yellow Gate Director."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ba's Han shu states: "The forbidden gate is called the Yellow Portal; eunuchs oversee it, hence the title Yellow Gate Director."

sentences.zh: 然則黃門郎給事黃闥之內，故曰黃門郎也。

translations.literal: Thus the Yellow Gate Attendant served within the Yellow Portal, and is therefore called Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the Yellow Gate Attendant served inside the Yellow Portal, which is why the title bears the name Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來員四人，秩六百石。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward the quota was four persons, rank six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward there were four posts, at the rank of six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 公車令，一人。

translations.literal: Imperial Carriage Director, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Carriage Director: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌受章奏。

translations.literal: In charge of receiving memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He received all written memorials.

sentences.zh: 秦有公車司馬令，屬衛尉，漢因之，掌宮南闕門。

translations.literal: Qin had an Imperial Carriage Master of Horse Director, subordinate to the Minister of Guards; Han followed this, in charge of the southern gate-tower of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin there was an Imperial Carriage Master of Horse, subordinate to the Minister of Guards; the Han kept the office, which controlled the southern gate-tower of the palace.

sentences.zh: 凡吏民上章，四方貢獻，及征詣公車者，皆掌之。

translations.literal: All officials and commoners submitting memorials, tribute from the four directions, and those summoned to the Imperial Carriage office were under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: He handled every memorial from officials and commoners, tribute arriving from all quarters, and anyone summoned to report at the Imperial Carriage office.

sentences.zh: 晉江左以來，直雲公車令。

translations.literal: From the Jin after crossing south, the title was simply Imperial Carriage Director.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, the office was called simply Imperial Carriage Director.

sentences.zh: 太醫令，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Physician Director, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Physician Director: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 《周官》為醫師，秦為太醫令，至二漢屬少府。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had the Physician Master; Qin made it Grand Physician Director; through both Han dynasties it belonged to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou placed physicians under a Physician Master; the Qin renamed the post Grand Physician Director; under both Han dynasties it fell under the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 太官令，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Steward Director, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Steward Director: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 《周官》為膳夫，秦為太官令，至漢屬少府。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had the Diet Master; Qin made it Grand Steward Director; through Han it belonged to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou had a Diet Master; the Qin renamed the post Grand Steward Director; under the Han it too belonged to the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 驊騮廄丞，一人。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Hualiu Stables, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Hualiu Stables: one office.

sentences.zh: 漢西京為龍馬長，漢東京為未央廄令，魏為驊騮令。

translations.literal: Western Han capital had Dragon Horse Chief; Eastern Han capital had Weiyang Stables Director; Wei had Hualiu Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Han capital the post was Dragon Horse Chief; at the Eastern Han capital it was Director of the Weiyang Stables; under the Wei it was Hualiu Director.

sentences.zh: 自公車令至此，隸侍中。

translations.literal: From the Imperial Carriage Director down to here, they were subordinate to the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: From the Imperial Carriage Director through these offices, all were subordinate to the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍，四人。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary: four offices.

sentences.zh: 掌侍左右。

translations.literal: In charge of attending left and right.
translations.idiomatic: They attended at the ruler's left and right.

sentences.zh: 秦置散騎，又置中常侍，散騎並乘輿車後；

translations.literal: Qin established Cavalier Attendants, and also established Regular Palace Attendants; Cavalier Attendants all rode behind the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: The Qin created Cavalier Attendants and also Regular Palace Attendants; the Cavalier Attendants all rode behind the imperial carriage;

sentences.zh: 中常侍得入禁中。

translations.literal: Regular Palace Attendants could enter the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: while the Regular Palace Attendants were allowed into the forbidden inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 皆無員，並為加官。

translations.literal: Both had no fixed quota and were supplementary offices.
translations.idiomatic: Neither had a fixed quota; both were supplementary appointments.

sentences.zh: 漢東京初省散騎，而中常侍因用宦者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Eastern Han capital the Cavalier Attendants were cut; Regular Palace Attendants then used eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Han capital the Cavalier Attendants were abolished, and Regular Palace Attendants came to be filled by eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，置散騎，合於中常侍，謂之散騎常侍，始以孟達補之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's Huangchu era, Cavalier Attendants were established, combined with Regular Palace Attendants, called Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; Meng Da was first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Wen of Wei's Huangchu reign, Cavalier Attendants were restored and merged with the Regular Palace Attendants under the title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; Meng Da received the first appointment.

sentences.zh: 久次者為祭酒散騎常侍，秩比二千石。

translations.literal: Those of long seniority became Libationer Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, rank equivalent to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The senior incumbent was styled Libationer Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, at the equivalent rank of two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍，四人。

translations.literal: Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication: four offices.

sentences.zh: 魏末散騎常侍又有在員外者，晉武帝使二人與散騎常侍通直，故謂之通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei some Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary were outside the quota; Emperor Wu of Jin had two persons communicate directly with the Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary, hence called Regular Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wei some Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary served outside the regular quota; Emperor Wu of Jin assigned two men to liaise directly with the regular incumbents, whence the title Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 晉江左置五人。

translations.literal: After the Jin crossed south, five were established.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south the quota was raised to five.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎常侍，魏末置，無員。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, established at the end of Wei, no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary: created late in the Wei, without a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎，四人。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant: four offices.

sentences.zh: 魏初與散騎常侍同置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei it was established together with Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei created the post at the same time as the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉散騎常侍、侍郎，與侍中、黃門侍郎共平尚書奏事，江左乃罷。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin, Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary and Attendants, together with Palace Attendants and Yellow Gate Attendants, jointly reviewed Secretariat memorials; after crossing south this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei and Jin, Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary and Cavalier Attendants, together with Palace Attendants and Yellow Gate Attendants, jointly reviewed Secretariat memorials; the Eastern Jin abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎侍郎，四人。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant for Direct Communication, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant for Direct Communication: four offices.

sentences.zh: 初晉武帝置員外散騎侍郎四人，元帝使二人與散騎侍郎通直，故謂之通直散騎侍郎，後增為四人。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Wu of Jin established four Supernumerary Cavalier Attendants; Emperor Yuan had two communicate directly with Cavalier Attendants, hence called Cavalier Attendants for Direct Communication; later increased to four.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin first appointed four Supernumerary Cavalier Attendants; Emperor Yuan assigned two to liaise directly with the regular Cavalier Attendants, whence the title Cavalier Attendant for Direct Communication; the quota was later fixed at four.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎，晉武帝置，無員。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, established by Emperor Wu of Jin, no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant: created by Emperor Wu of Jin, without a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 給事中，無員。

translations.literal: Attendant Within, no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within: no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 漢西京置。

translations.literal: Established at the Western Han capital.
translations.idiomatic: The office was created at the Western Han capital.

sentences.zh: 掌顧問應對，位次中常侍。

translations.literal: In charge of consultation and response, ranking below Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: They advised and answered the ruler, ranking just below the Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢東京省，魏世復置。

translations.literal: Cut at the Eastern Han capital; restored in the Wei era.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital abolished the post; the Wei restored it.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請，無員，亦不為官。

translations.literal: Court Supplicant, no fixed quota, and not counted as an office.
translations.idiomatic: Court Supplicant: no fixed quota and not treated as a regular office.

sentences.zh: 漢東京罷省三公、外戚、宗室、諸侯，多奉朝請。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital abolished the Three Dukes, consort kin, imperial clansmen, and feudal lords, and many became Court Supplicants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Han capital stripped the Three Dukes, consort kin, imperial clansmen, and feudal lords of their posts, many were made Court Supplicants instead.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請者，奉朝會請召而已。

translations.literal: Court Supplicants merely attended court assemblies when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: A Court Supplicant simply attended court when summoned to the assembly.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝亦以宗室外戚為奉車、駙馬、騎都尉，而奉朝請焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin also made imperial clansmen and consort kin Masters of the Carriage, Masters of the Stables, and Commandants of Cavalry, and they were Court Supplicants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin likewise appointed imperial clansmen and consort kin as Masters of the Carriage, Masters of the Stables, and Commandants of Cavalry, all with the status of Court Supplicant.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，以參軍為奉車都尉，掾、屬為駙馬都尉，行參軍、舍人為騎都尉，皆奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Prince of Jin, staff officers became Commandants of the Carriage, clerks and aides became Commandants of the Stables, acting staff officers and attendants became Commandants of Cavalry, all Court Supplicants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was still Prince of Jin, military aides became Commandants of the Carriage, clerks and aides became Commandants of the Stables, and acting aides and attendants became Commandants of Cavalry, each also holding Court Supplicant status.

sentences.zh: 後省奉車、騎都尉，唯留駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Later the Commandant of the Carriage and Commandant of Cavalry were cut; only Commandant of the Stables and Court Supplicant remained.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Commandant of the Carriage and Commandant of Cavalry were abolished, leaving only the Commandant of the Stables and the Court Supplicant.

sentences.zh: 永初已來，以奉朝請選雜，其尚主者唯拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: From Yongchu onward the selection of Court Supplicants was mixed; those marrying the emperor's daughter were only appointed Commandant of the Stables.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongchu reign onward Court Supplicant appointments grew heterogeneous; a man who married an imperial princess received only the Commandant of the Stables.

sentences.zh: 三都尉並漢武帝置。

translations.literal: All three commandants were established by Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: All three commandancies were created by Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，奉朝請省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian, Court Supplicant was cut.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiaojian era the Court Supplicant was abolished.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉、三都尉秩比二千石。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Stables and the three commandants had rank equivalent to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Stables and the three commandancies carried the equivalent rank of two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 中書令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat: one office.

sentences.zh: 中書監，一人。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Secretariat, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Secretariat: one office.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎，四人。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Attendant: four offices.

sentences.zh: 中書通事舍人，四人。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant for Communications, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Attendant for Communications: four offices.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝游後廷，始使宦者典尚書事，謂之中書謁者，置令、僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Han toured the rear apartments, he first had eunuchs manage Secretariat affairs, called Secretariat Chamberlains, establishing a director and vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han visited the rear apartments, he first put eunuchs in charge of Secretariat business under the title Secretariat Chamberlain, with a director and vice director.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，令弘恭，僕射石顯，秉勢用事，權傾內外。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time, Director Hong Gong and Vice Director Shi Xian wielded power and handled affairs, authority tilting inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan, Director Hong Gong and Vice Director Shi Xian seized power and ran affairs until their authority dominated court and capital alike.

sentences.zh: 成帝改中書謁者令曰中謁者令，罷僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng changed Secretariat Chamberlain Director to Central Chamberlain Director and abolished the vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng renamed the Secretariat Chamberlain Director as Central Chamberlain Director and abolished the vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 漢東京省中謁者令，而有中宮謁者令，非其職也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital cut the Central Chamberlain Director, but there was an Inner Palace Chamberlain Director, which was not the same duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital abolished the Central Chamberlain Director, though an Inner Palace Chamberlain Director remained—a separate office altogether.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝為王，置秘書令，典尚書奏事，又其任也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was king, he established a Palace Secretary Director to manage Secretariat memorials—again that duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was still king of Wei, he created a Palace Secretary Director to handle Secretariat memorials, reviving the same function.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初初，改為中書令，又置監，及通事郎，次黃門郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's Huangchu era, it was changed to Director of the Secretariat; a supervisor was also established, and Attendants for Communications, ranking below Yellow Gate Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Wen's Huangchu reign the post became Director of the Secretariat; a supervisor was added, along with Attendants for Communications ranking below the Yellow Gate Attendants.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎已署事過，通事乃奉以入，為帝省讀書可。

translations.literal: After the Yellow Gate Attendant had endorsed the matter, the Attendant for Communications presented it for entry, reading it for the emperor's approval.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow Gate Attendant had endorsed a document, the Attendant for Communications carried it in and read it aloud for the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 晉改曰中書侍郎，員四人。

translations.literal: Jin changed the title to Secretariat Attendant, quota four persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin renamed the post Secretariat Attendant and fixed the quota at four.

sentences.zh: 晉江左初，改中書侍郎曰通事郎，尋複為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Early after the Jin crossed south, Secretariat Attendant was changed to Attendant for Communications, soon restored to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Jin the Secretariat Attendant was briefly renamed Attendant for Communications, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 晉初置舍人一人，通事一人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin one attendant and one communications attendant were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Jin one secretariat attendant and one communications attendant were appointed.

sentences.zh: 江左初，合舍人通事謂之通事舍人，掌呈奏案章。

translations.literal: Early after crossing south, attendant and communications attendant were combined and called Attendant for Communications, in charge of presenting memorials and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the southward court the two posts were merged as Attendant for Communications, responsible for presenting memorials and case documents.

sentences.zh: 後省通事，中書差侍郎一人直西省，又掌詔命。

translations.literal: Later the communications attendant was cut; the Secretariat dispatched one attendant to staff the Western Office and also manage edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Later the separate communications attendant was abolished; the Secretariat detailed one attendant to the Western Office, which also handled imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 宋初又置通事舍人，而侍郎之任輕矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song the Attendant for Communications was again established, and the Attendant's duties became lighter.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Liu Song the Attendant for Communications was restored, and the Secretariat Attendant's duties grew lighter.

sentences.zh: 舍人直閤內，隸中書。

translations.literal: Attendants staffed the inner pavilion and were subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants were stationed inside the inner pavilion and reported to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其下有主事，本用武官，宋改用文吏。

translations.literal: Below them were clerks; originally military officers were used, but Song changed to civil clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath them were clerks; originally military officers filled the posts, but the Song replaced them with civil administrators.

sentences.zh: 秘書監，一人。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat: one office.

sentences.zh: 秘書丞，一人。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat: one office.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎，四人。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Attendant: four offices.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝延熹二年，置秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxi of Emperor Huan of Han, the Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Huan's Yanxi reign (159 CE) the court created the Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇甫規與張奐書雲「從兄秘書它何動靜」是也。

translations.literal: In Huangfu Gui's letter to Zhang Huan it says "How are my cousin the Palace Secretary's affairs?"—this is the same office.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Gui's letter to Zhang Huan asking "How are my cousin the Palace Secretary getting on?" refers to this same office.

sentences.zh: 應劭《漢官》曰：「秘書監一人，六百石。」

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "One Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, six hundred bushels."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices records: "One Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, at six hundred bushels."

sentences.zh: 後省。

translations.literal: Later it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The post was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝為魏王，置秘書令、秘書丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was king of Wei, he established Palace Secretary Director and Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was king of Wei he appointed a Palace Secretary Director and Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 秘書典尚書奏事。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat managed Secretariat memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretariat handled Secretariat memorials.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初初，置中書令，典尚書奏事，而秘書改令為監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's Huangchu era, Director of the Secretariat was established to manage Secretariat memorials, and the Palace Secretary Director was changed to supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Wen's Huangchu reign a Director of the Secretariat was created to handle memorials, and the Palace Secretary Director was demoted to supervisor.

sentences.zh: 後欲以何楨為秘書丞，而秘書先自有丞，乃以楨為秘書右丞。

translations.literal: Later they wished to make He Zhen Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat, but the Palace Secretariat already had an assistant director, so Zhen was made Right Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court wished to appoint He Zhen as assistant director, but the Palace Secretariat already had one, so Zhen was made Right Assistant Director instead.

sentences.zh: 後省。

translations.literal: Later it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The post was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 掌藝文圖籍。

translations.literal: In charge of literary works and maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw literary works, maps, and archival registers.

sentences.zh: 《周官》外史掌四方之志、三皇五帝之書，即其任也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had the Outer Scribe manage records of the four directions and books of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors—this is that duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Offices of Zhou the Outer Scribe kept records of the four quarters and writings of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors—the same responsibility.

sentences.zh: 漢西京圖籍所藏，有天府、石渠、蘭台、石室、延閣、廣內之府是也。

translations.literal: Where maps and registers were stored at the Western Han capital were the Heavenly Storehouse, Stone Canal, Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Extended Pavilion, and Broad Inner repositories.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Han capital the collections were housed in the Heavenly Storehouse, Stone Canal, Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Extended Pavilion, and Broad Inner repositories.

sentences.zh: 東京圖書在東觀。

translations.literal: At the Eastern capital, books were in the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the library stood in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝以秘書並中書，省監，謂丞為中書秘書丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin merged the Palace Secretariat with the Secretariat and cut the supervisor, calling the assistant director Secretariat–Palace Secretariat Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin merged the Palace Secretariat into the Directorate of the Secretariat, abolished the supervisor, and styled the assistant director the Secretariat–Palace Secretariat Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 惠帝複置著作郎一人，佐郎八人，掌國史。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui restored one Authoring Attendant and eight assistant attendants, in charge of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui restored one Authoring Attendant with eight assistants to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 周世左史記事，右史記言，即其任也。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era the left scribe recorded events and the right scribe recorded words—this is that duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou times the left scribe recorded events and the right scribe recorded speeches—the same division of labor.

sentences.zh: 漢東京圖籍在東觀，故使名儒碩學，著作東觀，撰述國史。

translations.literal: Eastern Han capital books were in the Eastern Pavilion, so eminent Confucians and great scholars authored at the Eastern Pavilion and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Eastern Han library lay in the Eastern Pavilion, leading scholars were sent there to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 著作之名，自此始也。

translations.literal: The title Authoring Attendant began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The title Authoring Attendant dates from this practice.

sentences.zh: 魏世隸中書。

translations.literal: In the Wei era it was subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei it reported to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉武世，繆征為中書著作郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Jin's time, Miao Zheng was Secretariat Authoring Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu of Jin's reign Miao Zheng served as Secretariat Authoring Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元康中，改隸秘書，後別自為省，而猶隸秘書。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era it was changed to be subordinate to the Palace Secretariat; later it was separately made its own office, yet still subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang era it was placed under the Palace Secretariat; later it became a separate bureau, though still nominally under the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 著作郎謂之大著作，專掌史任。

translations.literal: The Authoring Attendant was called Grand Author, exclusively in charge of historiographical duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Authoring Attendant was styled Grand Author and held sole responsibility for historical compilation.

sentences.zh: 晉制，著作佐郎始到職，必撰名臣傳一人。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, when an Assistant Authoring Attendant first took office, he had to compile one biography of a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin rules, a newly appointed Assistant Authoring Attendant had to draft one biography of a noted minister.

sentences.zh: 宋氏初，國朝始建，未有合撰者，此制遂替矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song house, when the dynasty was first established, there was no one to undertake the compilation together, and this regulation therefore lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu Song dynasty was first founded, no suitable compiler was available, and the rule fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍，一人。

translations.literal: General Who Commands the Army, one person.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Commands the Army: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌內軍。

translations.literal: In charge of the inner armies.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the inner armies.

sentences.zh: 漢有南北軍，衛京師。

translations.literal: Han had Northern and Southern Armies guarding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Han maintained Northern and Southern Armies to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 武帝置中壘校尉，掌北軍營。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu established the Colonel of the Central Rampart to manage the Northern Army camp.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu created the Colonel of the Central Rampart to command the Northern Army camp.

sentences.zh: 光武省中壘校尉，置北軍中候，監五校營。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu cut the Colonel of the Central Rampart and established the Northern Army Commandant to supervise the five camp commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu abolished the Colonel of the Central Rampart and created the Northern Army Commandant to supervise the five camp commandants.

sentences.zh: 魏武為丞相，相府自置領軍，非漢官也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was chancellor, the chancellor's office itself established a Commander of the Army—not a Han office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was chancellor, his staff created a Commander of the Army—a title outside the Han roster.

sentences.zh: 文帝即魏王位，魏始置領軍，主五校、中壘、武衛三營。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingship of Wei, Wei first established the Commander of the Army, commanding the five commandants, Central Rampart, and Martial Guard camps.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi became King of Wei, Wei first established the Commander of the Army to command the five commandants and the Central Rampart and Martial Guard camps.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝初省，使中軍將軍羊祜統二衛前後左右驍騎七軍營兵，即領軍之任也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Jin it was cut, and General of the Central Army Yang Hu was made to command the seven camp troops of the two guards, front and rear, left and right, and valiant cavalry—that was the Commander's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Early under Emperor Wu of Jin the post was abolished, and General of the Central Army Yang Hu was assigned to command the seven camp forces of the two guards, front and rear, left and right, and valiant cavalry—the Commander of the Army's responsibility.

sentences.zh: 祜遷罷，復置北軍中候。

translations.literal: When Hu was transferred and removed, the Northern Army Commandant was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hu was transferred and removed from office, the Northern Army Commandant was restored.

sentences.zh: 北軍中候置丞一人。

translations.literal: The Northern Army Commandant had one assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Army Commandant had one assistant director.

sentences.zh: 懷帝永嘉中，改曰中領軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era of Emperor Huai, it was changed to Central Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huai's Yongjia era (307–313 CE) the title was changed to Central Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 元帝永昌元年，復改曰北軍中候。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan, it was again changed to Northern Army Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Yuan's Yongchang reign (322 CE) it was again changed to Northern Army Commandant.

sentences.zh: 尋復為領軍。

translations.literal: Soon it was again made Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it was again styled Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 成帝世，復以為中候，而陶回居之。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Cheng, it was again made commandant, and Tao Hui held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng it was again made commandant, and Tao Hui held the office.

sentences.zh: 尋復為領軍。

translations.literal: Soon it was again made Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it was again styled Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 領軍今猶有南軍都督。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Army today still has a Southern Army Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Commander of the Army still retained a Southern Army Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍，一人。

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army, one person.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌外軍。

translations.literal: In charge of the outer armies.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the outer armies.

sentences.zh: 秦時護軍都尉，漢因之。

translations.literal: Under Qin there was a Commandant Who Protects the Army; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin created a Commandant Who Protects the Army; the Han kept the office.

sentences.zh: 陳平為護軍中尉，盡護諸將。

translations.literal: Chen Ping was Central Commandant Who Protects the Army and fully protected all generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping served as Central Commandant Who Protects the Army, overseeing all field commanders.

sentences.zh: 然則複以都尉為中尉矣。

translations.literal: Thus the commandant title was again made central commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the post was again styled a central commandant.

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩四年，以護軍都尉屬大司馬，于時複為都尉矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu, the Commandant Who Protects the Army was made subordinate to the Grand Marshal, and at that time it again became commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshou reign (119 BCE) the Commandant Who Protects the Army was placed under the Grand Marshal, and the title reverted to commandant.

sentences.zh: 《漢書·李廣傳》，廣為驍騎將軍，屬護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Han shu, Biography of Li Guang, Guang was General of Valiant Cavalry, subordinate to the General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu, Biography of Li Guang, records that Li Guang served as General of Valiant Cavalry under the General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 蓋護軍護諸將軍。

translations.literal: Thus the Protector of the Army protected all generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Protector of the Army, in short, oversaw all other generals.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽元年，更名護軍都尉曰司寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshou of Emperor Ai, the Commandant Who Protects the Army was renamed Minister of Corrections.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Ai's Yuanshou reign (2 BCE) the Commandant Who Protects the Army was renamed Minister of Corrections.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始元年，更名護軍都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping, it was renamed Commandant Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi reign (1 CE) the title was restored to Commandant Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 東京省，班固為大將軍中護軍，隸將軍莫府，非漢朝列職。

translations.literal: The Eastern capital cut the office; Ban Gu was Central Protector of the Army under the Grand General, subordinate to the general's staff, not a regular Han dynasty post.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital abolished the regular post; Ban Gu served as Central Protector of the Army on the Grand General's staff—a special appointment, not a standing Han office.

sentences.zh: 魏武為相，以韓浩為護軍，史奐為領軍，非漢官也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was chancellor, Han Hao was made Protector of the Army and Shi Huan was made Commander of the Army—neither a Han office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was chancellor he appointed Han Hao Protector of the Army and Shi Huan Commander of the Army—titles outside the Han roster.

sentences.zh: 建安十二年，改護軍為中護軍，領軍為中領軍，置長史、司馬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jian'an, Protector of the Army was changed to Central Protector of the Army, Commander of the Army to Central Commander of the Army, and chief clerks and masters of horse were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jian'an (207 CE) the Protector of the Army became Central Protector of the Army and the Commander of the Army became Central Commander of the Army, each with a chief clerk and master of horse.

sentences.zh: 魏初因置護軍，主武官選，隸領軍，晉世則不隸也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei the Protector of the Army was accordingly established, in charge of selecting military officers, subordinate to the Commander of the Army; in the Jin era it was no longer subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wei the Protector of the Army was restored to manage military appointments under the Commander of the Army; under the Jin it reported independently.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌元年，省護軍並領軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the Protector of the Army was cut and merged with the Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Yuan's Yongchang reign (322 CE) the Protector of the Army was abolished and merged into the Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧二年，復置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taining of Emperor Ming, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming's Taining reign (324 CE) the office was restored.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉江右領、護各領營兵；

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin in the south, the Commander and Protector each led camp troops;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei and Jin in the south, the Commander and Protector each headed their own camp troops;

sentences.zh: 江左以來，領軍不復別置營，總統二衛驍騎材官諸營，護軍猶別有營也。

translations.literal: Since crossing east of the Yangzi, the Commander of the Army no longer had a separate camp, but commanded all camps of the two guards, valiant cavalry, and skilled troops; the Protector of the Army still had its own camp.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, the Commander of the Army no longer maintained a separate camp but oversaw all camps of the two guards, valiant cavalry, and skilled troops; the Protector of the Army still kept an independent camp.

sentences.zh: 領、護資重者為領軍、護軍將軍，資輕者為中領軍、中護軍。

translations.literal: Those of heavier credentials were Commander and Protector Generals; those of lighter credentials were Central Commander and Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Senior appointees became General Who Commands the Army or General Who Protects the Army; junior appointees became Central Commander or Central Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 官屬有長史、司馬、功曹、主簿、五官。

translations.literal: Staff included chief clerk, master of horse, merit officer, chief recorder, and five officers.
translations.idiomatic: The staff comprised a chief clerk, master of horse, merit officer, chief recorder, and five section officers.

sentences.zh: 受命出征，則置參軍。

translations.literal: When ordered on campaign, staff officers were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign orders, military aides were added to the staff.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍，一人。

translations.literal: General of the Left Guard, one person.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Guard: one office.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍，一人。

translations.literal: General of the Right Guard, one person.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guard: one office.

sentences.zh: 二衛將軍掌宿衛營兵。

translations.literal: The two guard generals managed palace-guard camp troops.
translations.idiomatic: The two guard generals commanded the palace-guard camps.

sentences.zh: 二漢、魏不置。

translations.literal: Neither of the two Han dynasties nor Wei established them.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Han dynasty nor the Wei maintained these posts.

sentences.zh: 晉文帝為相國，相國府置中衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Jin was chancellor of state, the chancellor's office established a General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao was chancellor of state, his office created a General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 武帝初，分中衛置左右衛將軍，以羊琇為左衛，趙序為右衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu, the Central Guard was divided to establish Left and Right Guard generals; Yang Hu was Left Guard, Zhao Xu Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wu's reign the Central Guard was split into left and right; Yang Hu became General of the Left Guard and Zhao Xu General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 二衛江右有長史、司馬、功曹、主簿，江左無長史。

translations.literal: The two guards in the south had chief clerk, master of horse, merit officer, and chief recorder; east of the Yangzi they had no chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the southern Jin the two guards had chief clerks, masters of horse, merit officers, and chief recorders; after the move east of the Yangzi they had no chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍，漢武帝元光六年，李廣為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: General of Valiant Cavalry: in the sixth year of Yuanguang of Emperor Wu of Han, Li Guang was General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: General of Valiant Cavalry: in the sixth year of Emperor Wu's Yuanguang reign (129 BCE) Li Guang received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 魏世置為內軍，有營兵，高功者主之。

translations.literal: In the Wei era it was established as inner army, with camp troops; those of high merit held it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei it became an inner army with its own camp, reserved for officers of distinguished merit.

sentences.zh: 先有司馬、功曹、主簿，後省。

translations.literal: At first there were master of horse, merit officer, and chief recorder; later cut.
translations.idiomatic: It once had a master of horse, merit officer, and chief recorder, but these were later abolished.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍，漢武帝時，韓說為遊擊。

translations.literal: General of Mobile Attack: in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, Han Yue was Mobile Attack.
translations.idiomatic: General of Mobile Attack: under Emperor Wu of Han, Han Yue held the post.

sentences.zh: 是為六軍。

translations.literal: These were the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Together these formed the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍、右軍將軍、前軍將軍、後軍將軍。

translations.literal: General of the Left Army, General of the Right Army, General of the Forward Army, General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Army, General of the Right Army, General of the Forward Army, and General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝時，有左軍將軍，然則左軍魏官也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Wei there was a General of the Left Army; thus the Left Army was a Wei office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Wei there was already a General of the Left Army, showing it to be a Wei creation.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝初，置前軍、右軍；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Jin, the Forward Army and Right Army were established;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wu of Jin's reign the Forward Army and Right Army were created;

sentences.zh: 泰始八年，又置後軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taishi, the Rear Army was also established.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth year of the Taishi era (272 CE) the Rear Army was added.

sentences.zh: 是為四軍。

translations.literal: These were the Four Armies.
translations.idiomatic: These constituted the Four Armies.

sentences.zh: 左中郎將、右中郎將，秦官，漢因之。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Left and Right, Qin offices, Han followed.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Left and Right: Qin offices adopted by the Han.

sentences.zh: 與五官中郎將領三署郎，魏無三署郎，猶置其職。

translations.literal: Together with the General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household for All Five Offices they led the Three Offices gentlemen; Wei had no Three Offices gentlemen, yet still kept the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household for All Five Offices they commanded the Three Offices gentlemen; the Wei had no such gentlemen but retained the titles.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝省。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin cut them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin abolished them.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖大明中，又置。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, they were again established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, during the Daming era, they were restored.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉、步兵校尉、越騎校尉、長水校尉、射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavalry, Commandant of Foot Soldiers, Commandant of the Vanguard, Commandant of the Long River, Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry, Commandant of Foot Soldiers, Commandant of the Vanguard, Commandant of the Long River, and Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

sentences.zh: 五校並漢武帝置。

translations.literal: All five commandants were established by Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: All five commandancies were created by Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 屯騎、步兵掌上林苑門屯兵；

translations.literal: Cavalry and Foot Soldiers commandants managed garrison troops at the Shanglin Park gates;
translations.idiomatic: The Commandants of Cavalry and Foot Soldiers garrisoned the gates of the Shanglin Park;

sentences.zh: 越騎掌越人來降，因以為騎也；

translations.literal: the Vanguard managed Yue people who came to surrender and therefore became cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: the Vanguard commanded Yue tribesmen who had submitted and were organized as cavalry;

sentences.zh: 一說取其材力超越也。

translations.literal: one explanation says it took those whose talent and strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: another explanation holds that it recruited men of exceptional strength and skill.

sentences.zh: 長水掌長水宣曲胡騎。

translations.literal: Long River managed Long River Xuanqu Hu cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Long River commandant led Hu cavalry of the Long River and Xuanqu districts.

sentences.zh: 長水，胡部落名也。

translations.literal: Long River was the name of a Hu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Long River was the name of a non-Chinese tribal district.

sentences.zh: 胡騎屯宣曲觀下。

translations.literal: Hu cavalry were garrisoned below Xuanqu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Their cavalry were stationed below the Xuanqu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 韋曜曰：「長水校尉，典胡騎，廄近長水，故以為名。

translations.literal: Wei Yao says: "The Commandant of the Long River managed Hu cavalry; the stables were near Long River, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao writes: "The Commandant of the Long River oversaw Hu cavalry; the stables lay near the Long River, whence the title.

sentences.zh: 長水，蓋關中小水名也。」

translations.literal: Long River was probably the name of a small stream in Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Long River was likely a minor watercourse in the Guanzhong region."

sentences.zh: 射聲掌射聲士，聞聲則射之，故以為名。

translations.literal: Archers Who Shoot at Sound managed archers who shot when they heard a sound, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound led troops trained to shoot at a sound cue, which gave the office its name.

sentences.zh: 漢光武初，改屯騎為驍騎，越騎為青巾。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Guangwu of Han, Cavalry was changed to Valiant Cavalry, Vanguard to Green Headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Guangwu's reign the Commandant of Cavalry was renamed Valiant Cavalry and the Vanguard became Green Headcloth.

sentences.zh: 建武十五年，復舊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jianwu, the old names were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jianwu (39 CE) the original titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 漢東京五校，典宿衛士。

translations.literal: The five commandants of the Eastern Han capital managed palace-guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the five commandants commanded the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 自遊擊至五校，魏、晉逮于江左，初猶領營兵，並置司馬、功曹、主簿，後省。

translations.literal: From Mobile Attack down to the five commandants, through Wei and Jin to east of the Yangzi, at first they still led camp troops and all had masters of horse, merit officers, and chief recorders; later cut.
translations.idiomatic: From the General of Mobile Attack through the five commandants, under the Wei and Jin and after the move south, they initially still commanded camps with masters of horse, merit officers, and chief recorders, all later abolished.

sentences.zh: 二中郎將本不領營也。

translations.literal: The two generals of the gentlemen-of-the-household originally did not lead camps.
translations.idiomatic: The two Gentlemen-of-the-Household generals never commanded camps in the first place.

sentences.zh: 五營校尉，秩二千石。

translations.literal: The five camp commandants had rank of two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The five camp commandants held the rank of two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 虎賁中郎將，《周官》有虎賁氏。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Tiger Guard: the Offices of Zhou had the Tiger Guard clan.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Tiger Guard: the Offices of Zhou already listed a Tiger Guard corps.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝建元三年，始微行出遊，選材力之士執兵從送，期之諸門，故名期門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan of Emperor Wu of Han, he first traveled incognito; strong men bearing arms were selected to escort him, meeting him at the gates, hence called Gate-Meeting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Wu's Jianyuan reign (138 BCE) he first traveled incognito; stalwart men bearing arms were chosen to escort him and meet him at the palace gates, whence the name Gate-Meeting.

sentences.zh: 無員，多至千人。

translations.literal: No fixed quota, at most reaching one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed quota; the corps could number as many as a thousand.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始元年，更名曰虎賁郎，置中郎將領之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping, the name was changed to Tiger Guard Gentlemen, and a general of the gentlemen-of-the-household was established to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi reign (1 CE) they were renamed Tiger Guard Gentlemen, with a general of the gentlemen-of-the-household placed in command.

sentences.zh: 虎賁舊作虎奔，言如虎之奔走也。

translations.literal: Tiger Guard was formerly written Tiger Rush, meaning to rush like a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard was originally written Tiger Rush, evoking a tiger's charge.

sentences.zh: 王莽輔政，以古有勇士孟賁，故以奔為賁。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang assisted in government, because ancient times had the brave warrior Meng Ben, he changed rush to guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang held power he changed the character to ben, alluding to the ancient warrior Meng Ben.

sentences.zh: 比二千石。

translations.literal: Rank equivalent to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was equivalent to two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 冗從僕射，漢東京有中黃門冗從僕射，非其職也。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director: the Eastern Han capital had Inner Yellow Gate Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director, which was not this duty.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director: the Eastern Han capital had an Inner Yellow Gate Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director—a different office altogether.

sentences.zh: 魏世因其名而置冗從僕射。

translations.literal: In the Wei era, taking its name, the Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei borrowed the title to create the Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 羽林監，漢武帝太初元年，初置建章營騎，亦掌從送次期門，後更名羽林騎，置令、丞。

translations.literal: Forest of Feathers Inspector: in the first year of Taichu of Emperor Wu of Han, the Jianzhang Camp Cavalry was first established, also in charge of escort and meeting at the Gate-Meeting posts; later renamed Forest of Feathers Cavalry, with a director and assistant director established.
translations.idiomatic: Forest of Feathers Inspector: in the first year of Emperor Wu's Taichu reign (104 BCE) the Jianzhang Camp Cavalry was first created to escort the emperor and meet him at the Gate-Meeting posts; it was later renamed the Forest of Feathers Cavalry, with a director and assistant director.

sentences.zh: 宣帝令中郎將騎都尉監羽林，謂之羽林中郎將。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan ordered a general of the gentlemen-of-the-household and cavalry commandant to supervise the Forest of Feathers, called General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan ordered a Gentlemen-of-the-Household general and cavalry commandant to supervise the Forest of Feathers, styled General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Forest of Feathers.

sentences.zh: 漢東京又置羽林左監、羽林右監，至魏世不改。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital also established Left and Right Forest of Feathers Inspectors, unchanged through the Wei era.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital also created Left and Right Forest of Feathers Inspectors, and the arrangement continued unchanged under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 晉罷羽林中郎將，又省一監，置一監而已。

translations.literal: Jin abolished the General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Forest of Feathers, cut one inspector, and left only one inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin abolished the General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Forest of Feathers, reduced the two inspectors to one, and kept a single inspector.

sentences.zh: 自虎賁至羽林，是為三將。

translations.literal: From the Tiger Guard through the Forest of Feathers, these were the three generals.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tiger Guard through the Forest of Feathers, these were the three guard generals.

sentences.zh: 哀帝省。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai cut it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai abolished the office.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖永初初，復置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu of Emperor Gaozu of Song, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Liu Song's Yongchu reign (420 CE) it was restored.

sentences.zh: 江右領營兵，江左無復營兵。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi it commanded camp troops; east of the Yangzi there were no longer camp troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the south it still commanded camp troops; after the move east of the Yangzi it no longer did.

sentences.zh: 羽林監六百石。

translations.literal: The Forest of Feathers Inspector ranked at six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest of Feathers Inspector held the rank of six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 積射將軍。

translations.literal: General of Accumulated Archery.
translations.idiomatic: General of Accumulated Archery.

sentences.zh: 強弩將軍。

translations.literal: General of Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: General of Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝以路博德為強弩校尉，李沮為強弩將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han made Lu Bode Commandant of Strong Crossbows and Li Ju General of Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han appointed Lu Bode Commandant of Strong Crossbows and Li Ju General of Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以許延壽為強弩將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan made Xu Yanshou General of Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan appointed Xu Yanshou General of Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 強弩將軍至東漢為雜號，前漢至魏無積射。

translations.literal: General of Strong Crossbows by the Eastern Han was a miscellaneous title; from Former Han through Wei there was no Accumulated Archery.
translations.idiomatic: By the Eastern Han the General of Strong Crossbows was a miscellaneous title; from the Former Han through the Wei there was no General of Accumulated Archery.

sentences.zh: 晉太康十年，立射營、弩營，置積射、強弩將軍主之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang of Jin, archery and crossbow camps were established, and Generals of Accumulated Archery and Strong Crossbows were placed in command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Taikang era (289 CE) the Jin created separate archery and crossbow camps under the two generals.

sentences.zh: 自驍騎至強弩將軍，先並各置一人；

translations.literal: From Valiant Cavalry to General of Strong Crossbows, at first each had one person established;
translations.idiomatic: From the General of Valiant Cavalry through the General of Strong Crossbows, each post initially had a single appointee;

sentences.zh: 宋太宗泰始以來，多以軍功得此官，今並無復員。

translations.literal: Since Taishi of Emperor Taizong of Song, many obtained this office through military merit; now all no longer have fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Xiaowu's Taishi era, many men won these posts through military merit; today none retain a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍、殿中司馬督。

translations.literal: Palace Hall General, Palace Hall Master of Horse Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Hall General and Palace Hall Master-of-Horse Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝時，殿內宿衛，號曰三部司馬，置此二官，分隸左右二衛。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Jin's time, inner-palace night guards were called the Three Departments Masters of Horse; these two offices were established, divided subordinate to the left and right guards.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Jin the inner palace guards were organized as the Three Departments of Masters of Horse; these two offices were created, each reporting to one of the two guards.

sentences.zh: 江右初，員十人。

translations.literal: Early in the south, quota ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the southern court the quota was ten.

sentences.zh: 朝會宴饗，則將軍戎服，直侍左右，夜開城諸門，則執白虎幡監之。

translations.literal: At court assemblies and banquets, the general wore military dress and attended directly left and right; at night when opening the city gates, he held the white tiger banner to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies and banquets the general wore armor and stood at the ruler's side; at night, when the city gates were opened, he bore the white tiger banner to supervise the watch.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元中，改選，以門閥居之。

translations.literal: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, selection was changed so that those of eminent clans held the posts.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu's Taixuan era the posts were reserved for men of eminent lineage.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖永初初，增為二十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu of Emperor Gaozu of Song, increased to twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Gaozu's Yongchu reign the quota was raised to twenty.

sentences.zh: 其後過員者，謂之殿中員外將軍、員外司馬督。

translations.literal: Those beyond quota afterward were called Supernumerary Palace Hall General and Supernumerary Master of Horse Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Additional appointees beyond the quota were styled Supernumerary Palace Hall General and Supernumerary Master-of-Horse Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 其後並無復員。

translations.literal: Afterward all no longer had fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Later these posts too lost their fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍，無員。

translations.literal: General of Martial Guard, no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: General of Martial Guard: no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 初，魏王始置武衛中郎將，文帝踐阼，改為衛將軍，主禁旅，如今二衛，非其任也。

translations.literal: At first, when the king of Wei was established, Martial Guard General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household was created; when Emperor Wen ascended, it was changed to Guard General, in charge of forbidden troops, like today's two guards—not the same duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was still king of Wei he created a Martial Guard General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household; after Emperor Wen's accession it became Guard General, commanding the forbidden troops much like today's two guards—a distinct office.

sentences.zh: 晉氏不常置。

translations.literal: The Jin house did not regularly establish it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin did not keep the post in regular use.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖大明中，複置，代殿中將軍之任，比員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, it was restored, replacing the Palace Hall General's duty, comparable to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, during the Daming era, it was restored to replace the Palace Hall General, with standing comparable to a Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武騎常侍，無員。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary of Martial Cavalry, no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary of Martial Cavalry: no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 漢西京官。

translations.literal: Office of the Western Han capital.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Western Han capital office.

sentences.zh: 車駕游獵，常從射猛獸。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured on the hunt, they constantly followed to shoot fierce beasts.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial hunting excursions they rode alongside the emperor to shoot wild beasts.

sentences.zh: 後漢、魏、晉不置。

translations.literal: Later Han, Wei, and Jin did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han, Wei, and Jin did not maintain the post.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖大明中，復置。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, during the Daming era, it was restored.

sentences.zh: 比奉朝請。

translations.literal: Comparable to Court Supplicant.
translations.idiomatic: Its standing was comparable to that of a Court Supplicant.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞，一人。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌奏劾不法。

translations.literal: In charge of memorializing and impeaching unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne and impeached unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 秦時御史大夫有二丞，其一曰御史丞，其二曰御史中丞。

translations.literal: Under Qin the Censor-in-Chief had two assistants; one was called Assistant Censor, the other Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin the Censor-in-Chief had two assistants: the Assistant Censor and the Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 殿中蘭臺祕書圖籍在焉，而中丞居之。

translations.literal: The Orchid Terrace palace secretariat maps and registers were kept there, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief resided there.
translations.idiomatic: The Orchid Terrace palace secretariat, maps, and registers were kept there, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief had his seat there.

sentences.zh: 外督部刺史，內領侍御史，受公卿奏事，舉劾按章。

translations.literal: Externally he supervised regional inspectors; internally he commanded attendant imperial secretaries, received memorials from ministers and grandees, and impeached according to the documents.
translations.idiomatic: Externally he supervised regional inspectors; internally he commanded attendant imperial secretaries, received memorials from ministers and grandees, and brought charges according to the records.

sentences.zh: 時中丞亦受奏事，然則分有所掌也。

translations.literal: At the time the Vice Censor-in-Chief also received memorials, and thus each had a separate charge.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Vice Censor-in-Chief also received memorials, so their duties were divided.

sentences.zh: 成帝綏和元年，更名御史大夫為大司空，置長史，而中丞官職如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Suihe of Emperor Cheng, the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works, a chief clerk was established, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief's duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Cheng's Suihe reign (7 BCE) the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works and given a chief clerk, while the Vice Censor-in-Chief's duties remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平二年，復為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianping of Emperor Ai, it was again made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ai's Jianping reign (5 BCE) the title was restored to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元壽二年，復為大司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou, it was again made Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou (1 BCE) it was again made Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 而中丞出外為御史臺主，名御史長史。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief went outside to head the Censorate and was titled Chief Clerk of the Censors.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Censor-in-Chief then headed the Censorate from outside and was styled Chief Clerk of the Censors.

sentences.zh: 光武還曰中丞，又屬少府。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu restored the title Vice Censor-in-Chief and again made it subordinate to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu restored the title Vice Censor-in-Chief and again placed the office under the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 獻帝時，更置御史大夫，自置長史一人，不復領中丞也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xian, the Censor-in-Chief was re-established, with one chief clerk of its own, and no longer commanded the Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xian the Censor-in-Chief was re-established with its own chief clerk and no longer commanded the Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 漢東京御史中丞遇尚書丞郎，則中丞止車執版揖，而丞郎坐車舉手禮之而已。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Han capital, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief met Secretariat assistant directors and attendants, the Vice Censor-in-Chief stopped his carriage, held his tablet, and bowed, while the assistant directors and attendants remained seated in their carriages and merely raised their hands in salute.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief met Secretariat assistant directors and attendants, he stopped his carriage, held his tablet, and bowed, while they remained seated in their carriages and merely raised their hands in salute.

sentences.zh: 不知此制何時省。

translations.literal: It is not known when this regulation was cut.
translations.idiomatic: When this regulation was abolished is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 中丞每月二十五日，繞行宮垣白壁。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of each month the Vice Censor-in-Chief circled the palace walls and white ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of each month the Vice Censor-in-Chief made a circuit of the palace walls and white ramparts.

sentences.zh: 史臣按漢志執金吾每月三繞行宮城，疑是省金吾，以此事併中丞。

translations.literal: The historian comments: the Han Treatise records that the Commandant of the Metropolitan Convoy circled the palace city three times each month; it is suspected that when the Commandant was cut, this duty was merged into the Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: the Han Treatise records that the Commandant of the Metropolitan Convoy circled the palace city three times each month; it is likely that when that office was abolished, the duty was transferred to the Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 中丞秩千石。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief ranked at one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Censor-in-Chief held the rank of one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史，掌舉劾官品第六已上。

translations.literal: Imperial Secretary Attendant Who Drafts Documents, in charge of impeaching officials of rank six and above.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Secretary Attendant Who Drafts Documents: he impeached officials from the sixth rank upward.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝齋居決事，令禦史二人治書，因謂之治書禦史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan of Han fasted and dwelt apart to decide affairs, he ordered two imperial secretaries to draft documents, hence called Imperial Secretary Who Drafts Documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan fasted in seclusion to decide state affairs, he assigned two imperial secretaries to draft documents, whence the title Imperial Secretary Who Drafts Documents.

sentences.zh: 漢東京使明法律者為之，天下讞疑事，則以法律當其是非。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital had those versed in law serve; for doubtful cases throughout the realm, they applied the law to determine right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital legal specialists held the post; for doubtful cases empire-wide they judged right and wrong by the code.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，則分掌侍御史所掌諸曹，若尚書二丞也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, they divided management of the various bureaus under the attendant imperial secretary, like the two assistant directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin onward they divided among themselves the bureaus once overseen by the attendant imperial secretaries, much like the two assistant directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 侍御史，于周為柱下史。

translations.literal: Attendant Imperial Secretary: under the Zhou it was Censor Beneath the Pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Imperial Secretary: under the Zhou the office was called Censor Beneath the Pillars.

sentences.zh: 《周官》有禦史，掌治令，亦其任也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had Imperial Secretaries managing ordinances—this too was that duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou already listed Imperial Secretaries who managed ordinances—the same responsibility.

sentences.zh: 秦置侍御史，漢因之。

translations.literal: Qin established Attendant Imperial Secretaries; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin created Attendant Imperial Secretaries, and the Han kept the institution.

sentences.zh: 二漢員並十五人。

translations.literal: Both Han dynasties had a quota of fifteen persons each.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han dynasties the quota stood at fifteen.

sentences.zh: 掌察舉非法，受公卿奏事，有違失者舉劾之。

translations.literal: They managed inspection and impeachment of illegal acts, received memorials from ministers and grandees, and impeached those who had violations or faults.
translations.idiomatic: They investigated and impeached unlawful conduct, received memorials from ministers and grandees, and brought charges against offenders.

sentences.zh: 凡有五曹，一曰令曹，掌律令；

translations.literal: In all there were five bureaus: first, the Bureau of Ordinances, managing statutes and ordinances;
translations.idiomatic: There were five bureaus in all: first, the Bureau of Ordinances, which handled statutes and ordinances;

sentences.zh: 二曰印曹，掌刻印，三曰供曹，掌齋祠；

translations.literal: second, the Bureau of Seals, managing seal carving; third, the Bureau of Offerings, managing fasting sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Bureau of Seals, which carved official seals; third, the Bureau of Offerings, which managed fasting sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 四曰尉馬曹，掌官廄馬；

translations.literal: fourth, the Bureau of Stable Horses, managing official stable horses;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Bureau of Stable Horses, which oversaw the government stables;

sentences.zh: 五曰乘曹，掌護駕。

translations.literal: fifth, the Bureau of Escort, managing protection of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: and fifth, the Bureau of Escort, which guarded the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 魏置禦史八人，有治書曹，掌度支運，課第曹，掌考課，不知其餘曹也。

translations.literal: Wei established eight Imperial Secretaries; there was the Bureau of Drafting Documents, managing expenditure and transport, and the Bureau of Performance Evaluation, managing merit assessment—the other bureaus are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei appointed eight Imperial Secretaries, with a Bureau of Drafting Documents to manage expenditure and transport and a Bureau of Performance Evaluation to conduct merit reviews; the remaining bureaus are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝凡有吏曹、課第曹、直事曹、印曹、中都督曹、外都督曹、媒曹、符節曹、水曹、中旂曹、營軍曹、算曹、法曹，凡十三曹，而置禦史九人。

translations.literal: The Western Jin court in all had the Personnel Bureau, Performance Evaluation Bureau, Direct Affairs Bureau, Seal Bureau, Internal Commandery Superintendent Bureau, External Commandery Superintendent Bureau, Matchmaking Bureau, Credentials Bureau, Water Bureau, Central Banner Bureau, Camp Army Bureau, Calculation Bureau, and Law Bureau—thirteen bureaus in all—and established nine Imperial Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Jin court there were thirteen bureaus in all: Personnel, Performance Evaluation, Direct Affairs, Seals, Internal Commandery Superintendent, External Commandery Superintendent, Matchmaking, Credentials, Water, Central Banners, Camp Army, Calculation, and Law—with nine Imperial Secretaries appointed.

sentences.zh: 晉江左初，省課第曹，置庫曹，掌廄牧牛馬市租。

translations.literal: Early in the Jin south of the Yangzi, the Performance Evaluation Bureau was cut and the Storehouse Bureau was established, managing stable herds, cattle and horses, and market taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Jin the Performance Evaluation Bureau was abolished and a Storehouse Bureau was created to manage stable herds, livestock, and market taxes.

sentences.zh: 後複分庫曹，置外左庫、內左庫二曹。

translations.literal: Later the Storehouse Bureau was again divided, and the External Left Storehouse and Internal Left Storehouse bureaus were established.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Storehouse Bureau was split into two offices, the External Left Storehouse and the Internal Left Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖元嘉中，省外左庫，而內左庫直雲左庫。

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia era of the Liu Song, the External Left Storehouse was cut, and the Internal Left Storehouse was simply called the Left Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liu Song Yuanjia era the External Left Storehouse was abolished, and the Internal Left Storehouse was renamed simply the Left Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明中，複置。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu, it was again established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, during the Daming era, it was restored.

sentences.zh: 廢帝景和元年又省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe of the Deposed Emperor it was again cut.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe under the Deposed Emperor it was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 順帝初，省營軍併水曹，省算曹併法曹，吏曹不置御史，凡十御史焉。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shun's reign, the Camp Army and Water bureaus were cut; the Calculation Bureau was cut and merged with the Law Bureau; the Personnel Bureau had no Imperial Secretary appointed—in all there were ten Imperial Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shun's reign the Camp Army and Water bureaus were abolished, the Calculation Bureau was merged into the Law Bureau, and the Personnel Bureau went without an Imperial Secretary, leaving ten Imperial Secretaries in all.

sentences.zh: 魏又有殿中侍御史二人，蓋是蘭臺遣二御史居殿內察非法也。

translations.literal: Wei also had two Attendant Imperial Secretaries Within the Palace—probably the Orchid Terrace dispatching two Imperial Secretaries to dwell within the palace halls and inspect illegal acts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei also maintained two Attendant Imperial Secretaries Within the Palace, evidently two Imperial Secretaries dispatched by the Orchid Terrace to serve inside the palace and watch for violations.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝四人，江左二人。

translations.literal: The Western Jin court had four persons; south of the Yangzi, two.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Jin court there were four; after the move south, two.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢有符節令，隸少府，領符璽郎、符節令史。

translations.literal: Qin and Han had a Director of Credentials, subordinate to the Privy Treasurer, commanding Credential Seal Gentlemen and Credential Director Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin and Han there was a Director of Credentials, subordinate to the Privy Treasurer, with Credential Seal Gentlemen and credential clerks under his command.

sentences.zh: 蓋《周禮》典瑞、掌節之任也。

translations.literal: Probably this was the duty of Keeper of Regalia and Bearer of Staves in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: This was probably the same function as the Keeper of Regalia and Bearer of Staves in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 漢至魏別為一台，位次禦史中丞，掌授節、銅虎符、竹使符。

translations.literal: From Han through Wei it became a separate bureau, ranking next after the Palace Deputy Imperial Secretary, managing the bestowal of staffs of authority, bronze tiger tallies, and bamboo envoy tallies.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han through the Wei it became an independent bureau ranking just below the Palace Deputy Imperial Secretary, responsible for issuing staffs of authority, bronze tiger tallies, and bamboo envoy tallies.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始九年，省並蘭台，置符節禦史掌其事焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, it was cut and merged into the Orchid Terrace, and an Imperial Secretary of Credentials was established to manage its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin the bureau was abolished and absorbed into the Orchid Terrace, and an Imperial Secretary of Credentials was appointed to handle its duties.

sentences.zh: 謁者僕射，一人。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌大拜授及百官班次。

translations.literal: He managed major investitures and the order of ranks among the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw major investiture ceremonies and the ceremonial order of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 領謁者十人。

translations.literal: He commanded ten Attendants Who Petition.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded ten Attendants Who Petition.

sentences.zh: 謁者掌小拜授及報章。

translations.literal: Attendants Who Petition managed minor investitures and presentation of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendants Who Petition handled minor investitures and the delivery of memorials.

sentences.zh: 蓋秦官也。

translations.literal: Probably this was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: The office probably dated from the Qin.

sentences.zh: 謁，請也。

translations.literal: Ye means to request.
translations.idiomatic: Ye means to request or petition.

sentences.zh: 應氏《漢官》曰，堯以試舜，賓於四門，是其職也。

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says that when Yao tested Shun, he received guests at the Four Gates—this was that duty.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices states that when Yao tested Shun by receiving guests at the Four Gates, that was this same function.

sentences.zh: 秦世謁者七十人，漢因之。
