translations.literal: In the Qin age there were seventy Attendants Who Petition; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin there were seventy Attendants Who Petition, and the Han kept the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 後漢《百官志》，謁者僕射掌奉引。

translations.literal: The Later Han Records of Officials states that the Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition managed escort and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Later Han Records of Officials, the Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition led escort and presentation at court.

sentences.zh: 和帝世，陳郡何熙為謁者僕射，贊拜殿中，音動左右。

translations.literal: In Emperor He's reign, He Xi of Chen commandery served as Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition; when he intoned the ceremonial salutation in the hall, his voice moved those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor He's reign He Xi of Chen commandery served as Vice Director of Attendants Who Petition; when he intoned the ceremonial salutation in the hall, his voice filled the chamber.

sentences.zh: 然則又掌唱贊。

translations.literal: Thus he also managed ceremonial acclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Evidently the office also included leading ceremonial acclamation.

sentences.zh: 有常侍謁者五人，謁者則置三十五人，半減西京也。

translations.literal: There were five Regular Attendants Who Petition; Attendants Who Petition were established at thirty-five persons—half the Western Han capital quota.
translations.idiomatic: There were five Regular Attendants Who Petition and thirty-five Attendants Who Petition in all—half the number at the Western Han capital.

sentences.zh: 二漢並隸光祿勳。

translations.literal: Both Han dynasties placed them subordinate to the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han dynasties they were subordinate to the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 魏世置謁者十人。

translations.literal: In the Wei era ten Attendants Who Petition were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei the quota was fixed at ten Attendants Who Petition.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝省僕射，以謁者隸蘭臺。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin cut the vice director and placed Attendants Who Petition subordinate to the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin abolished the vice directorship and placed the Attendants Who Petition under the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 江左復置僕射，後又省。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi the vice director was again established, and later again cut.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south the vice directorship was restored, then abolished again.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖大明中，復置。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, during the Daming era, it was restored.

sentences.zh: 秩比千石。

translations.literal: Rank equivalent to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was equivalent to one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 都水使者，一人。

translations.literal: Commissioner for Waterways, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner for Waterways: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌舟航及運部。

translations.literal: He managed river craft and the transport department.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw river craft and the transport department.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢有都水長、丞，主陂池灌溉，保守河渠，屬太常。

translations.literal: Qin and Han had Directors and Assistant Directors for Waterways, managing reservoirs and irrigation, maintaining and guarding rivers and canals, subordinate to the Grand Master of Splendid Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin and Han there were Directors and Assistant Directors for Waterways who managed reservoirs and irrigation, maintained rivers and canals, and reported to the Grand Master of Splendid Rites.

sentences.zh: 漢東京省都水，置河堤謁者，魏因之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital cut the Directorate for Waterways and established Attendants Who Petition for River Dikes; Wei followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital abolished the Directorate for Waterways and created Attendants Who Petition for River Dikes; the Wei kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 漢世水衡都尉主上林苑，魏世主天下水軍舟船器械。

translations.literal: In Han times the Commandant of Water Balance managed the Shanglin Park; in Wei times he managed the empire's naval forces, boats, and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han the Commandant of Water Balance oversaw the Shanglin Park; under the Wei he commanded the empire's naval forces, ships, and equipment.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝省水衡，置都水使者，而河堤為都水官屬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin cut the Commandant of Water Balance and established the Commissioner for Waterways, while River Dike Attendants Who Petition became subordinates of the waterway office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin abolished the Commandant of Water Balance and created the Commissioner for Waterways, with the River Dike Attendants Who Petition placed among his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 有參軍二人，謁者一人，令史減置無常員。

translations.literal: There were two staff officers and one Attendant Who Petition; clerks were reduced in number and had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included two military aides and one Attendant Who Petition; clerks were reduced and had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝有參軍而無謁者，謁者則江左置也。

translations.literal: The Western Jin court had staff officers but no Attendants Who Petition; Attendants Who Petition were established south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Jin court there were military aides but no Attendants Who Petition; the attendant post was created only after the move south.

sentences.zh: 懷帝永嘉六年，胡入洛陽，都水使者爰浚先出督運得免。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai, when the barbarians entered Luoyang, Commissioner for Waterways Yuan Jun went out first to supervise transport and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai, when invaders entered Luoyang, Commissioner for Waterways Yuan Jun had already gone out to supervise transport and so escaped.

sentences.zh: 然則武帝置職，便掌運矣。

translations.literal: Thus when Emperor Wu established the office, it already managed transport.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from the moment Emperor Wu created the post it already controlled transport.

sentences.zh: 江左省河隄。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi the River Dike office was cut.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south the River Dike office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 太子少傅，一人。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 傅，古官也。

translations.literal: Tutor was an ancient office.
translations.idiomatic: The tutorship was an ancient office.

sentences.zh: 《文王世子》曰：「凡三王教世子，太傅在前，少傅在後，並以輔導為職。」

translations.literal: Records of the Heir of King Wen says: "In general the Three Dynasties taught the heir, the Grand Tutor going before and the Junior Tutor following after, both taking guidance and instruction as their duty."
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Heir of King Wen states: "When the Three Dynasties instructed the heir, the Grand Tutor walked ahead and the Junior Tutor behind, both charged with guidance and instruction."

sentences.zh: 漢高帝九年，以叔孫通為太子太傅，位次太常。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Emperor Gaozu of Han, Shusun Tong was made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, ranking next after the Grand Master of Splendid Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Emperor Gaozu's reign Shusun Tong was appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, ranking just below the Grand Master of Splendid Rites.

sentences.zh: 二漢並無丞。

translations.literal: Both Han dynasties had no assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han dynasties there were no assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 魏世無東宮，然則晉氏置丞也。

translations.literal: In the Wei era there was no Eastern Palace; thus the Jin house established assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had no Eastern Palace establishment, so the Jin were the ones who added assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始五年，詔太子拜太傅、少傅，如弟子事師之禮；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict ordered that when the crown prince paid respects to the Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor, it should follow the ritual by which a disciple serves a teacher;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin an edict prescribed that the crown prince greet the Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor with the ceremony a disciple owes a teacher;

sentences.zh: 二傅不得上疏曲敬。

translations.literal: the two tutors could not submit memorials with indirect respectful forms.
translations.idiomatic: and the two tutors were forbidden to address him through memorials with the oblique forms of respect.

sentences.zh: 二傅並有功曹、主簿、五官。

translations.literal: Both tutors had merit officers, chief recorders, and five department heads.
translations.idiomatic: Each tutor had a merit officer, chief recorder, and five department heads on staff.

sentences.zh: 太傅中二千石，少傅二千石。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor ranked at middle two thousand bushels; the Junior Tutor at two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor held the rank of middle two thousand bushels and the Junior Tutor that of two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事，一人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Steward, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Steward: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 職比臺尚書令、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Duties comparable to Secretariat Director of the Terrace and General Who Commands the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His standing was comparable to that of the Secretariat Director of the Terrace and the General Who Commands the Army.

sentences.zh: 詹，省也。

translations.literal: Steward means to oversee.
translations.idiomatic: "Steward" means to oversee.

sentences.zh: 漢西京則太子門大夫、庶子、洗馬、舍人屬二傅，率更令、家令、僕、衞率屬詹事。

translations.literal: At the Western Han capital, the crown prince Gate Grand Master, Attendants to the Heir, Groom-in-Waiting, and Household Gentlemen belonged to the two tutors; the Director of Chastisement, Household Steward, Steward, and Commandant of the Guard belonged to the Steward.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Han capital the crown prince Gate Grand Master, Attendants to the Heir, Groom-in-Waiting, and Household Gentlemen reported to the two tutors, while the Director of Chastisement, Household Steward, Steward, and Commandant of the Guard reported to the Crown Prince Steward.

sentences.zh: 皆秦官也。

translations.literal: All were Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: All were offices of Qin origin.

sentences.zh: 後漢省詹事，太子官屬悉屬少傅，而太傅不復領官屬。

translations.literal: The Later Han cut the Steward; all crown prince staff belonged to the Junior Tutor, and the Grand Tutor no longer commanded staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han abolished the Steward; all crown prince staff then reported to the Junior Tutor, and the Grand Tutor no longer commanded subordinates.

sentences.zh: 晉初太子官屬通屬二傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, crown prince staff generally belonged to the two tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin, crown prince staff generally reported to the two tutors.

sentences.zh: 咸寧元年，復置詹事，二傅不復領官屬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning, the Steward was restored, and the two tutors no longer commanded staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianning (275 CE) the Steward was restored, and the two tutors no longer commanded subordinates.

sentences.zh: 詹事二千石。

translations.literal: The Steward ranked at two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince Steward held the rank of two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 家令，一人。

translations.literal: Household Steward, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Household Steward: one office.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 晉世置。

translations.literal: Established in the Jin era.
translations.idiomatic: The office was created under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 漢世太子食湯沐邑十縣，家令主之。

translations.literal: In Han times the crown prince received income from ten counties as bathing and fief lands; the Household Steward managed them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han the crown prince drew revenue from ten bathing-and-fief counties, which the Household Steward administered.

sentences.zh: 又主刑獄飲食，職比廷尉、司農、少府。

translations.literal: He also managed punishments, prisons, and food and drink, duties comparable to the Commandant of Justice, Minister of Finance, and Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He also oversaw punishments, prisons, and provisions, with duties comparable to those of the Commandant of Justice, Minister of Finance, and Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 漢東京主食官令。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital placed the Master of Victuals in charge.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the Master of Victuals held that responsibility.

sentences.zh: 食官令，晉世自為官，不復屬家令。

translations.literal: The Master of Victuals in the Jin era became an office in its own right and no longer belonged to the Household Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin the Master of Victuals became an independent office and no longer reported to the Household Steward.

sentences.zh: 率更令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of Chastisement, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Chastisement: one office.

sentences.zh: 主宮殿門戶及賞罰事，職如光祿勳、衛尉。

translations.literal: He managed palace halls, gates, and doors and matters of reward and punishment; duties like those of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the palace halls, gates, and doors and handled rewards and punishments, with duties comparable to those of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and the Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢東京掌庶子、舍人，晉世則不也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital had him manage Attendants to the Crown Prince and Household Gentlemen; in the Jin era he did not.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital he also commanded Attendants to the Crown Prince and household gentlemen; under the Jin he did not.

sentences.zh: 自漢至晉，家令在率更下；

translations.literal: From Han through Jin, the Household Steward ranked below the Director of Chastisement;
translations.idiomatic: From the Han through the Jin the Household Steward ranked below the Director of Chastisement;

sentences.zh: 宋則居上。

translations.literal: under Song he ranked above.
translations.idiomatic: under the Liu Song he ranked above.

sentences.zh: 僕，一人。

translations.literal: Steward, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Steward: one office.

sentences.zh: 漢世太子五日一朝，非入朝日，遣僕及中允旦入請問起居，主車馬、親族，職如太僕、宗正。

translations.literal: In Han times the crown prince had audience every five days; on days when he did not enter court, the Steward and the Palace Attendant Within were sent at dawn to inquire after the emperor's health; they managed horses and carriages and the imperial clan, duties like those of the Grand Master of the Stud and Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han the crown prince attended court every five days; on other days the Steward and the Palace Attendant Within were sent at dawn to inquire after the emperor's health. They managed horses, carriages, and the imperial clan, with duties comparable to those of the Grand Master of the Stud and the Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 自家令至僕，為太子三卿。

translations.literal: From the Household Steward down to the Steward, these were the crown prince's Three Directors.
translations.idiomatic: From the Household Steward through the Steward, these three offices formed the crown prince's Three Directors.

sentences.zh: 三卿，秩千石。

translations.literal: The Three Directors had rank of one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Directors held the rank of one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 門大夫，二人。

translations.literal: Gate Masters, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Gate Masters: two offices.

sentences.zh: 漢東京置，職如中郎將，分掌遠近表箋。

translations.literal: Established at the Eastern Han capital, duties like those of a General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, dividing management of near and distant memorials and letters.
translations.idiomatic: Created at the Eastern Han capital, with duties like those of a General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, they divided responsibility for incoming memorials near and far.

sentences.zh: 秩六百石。

translations.literal: Rank of six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 中庶子，四人。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince: four offices.

sentences.zh: 職如侍中。

translations.literal: Duties like those of a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Their duties were like those of a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢東京員五人，晉減為四人。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital had a quota of five persons; Jin reduced it to four.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the quota was five; the Jin reduced it to four.

sentences.zh: 秩六百石。

translations.literal: Rank of six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 中舍人，四人。

translations.literal: Attendants Within to the Crown Prince, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Within to the Crown Prince: four offices.

sentences.zh: 漢東京太子官屬有中允之職，在中庶子下，洗馬上，疑若今中書舍人矣。

translations.literal: Among the Eastern Han capital crown prince's staff there was the duty of Palace Attendant Within, below the Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince and above the Groom-in-Waiting—probably like today's Secretariat Attendants Within.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Eastern Han crown prince's staff there was a Palace Attendant Within, ranking below the Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince and above the Groom-in-Waiting—likely the predecessor of today's Secretariat Attendants Within.

sentences.zh: 中舍人，晉初置，職如黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Attendants Within to the Crown Prince were established at the beginning of Jin, with duties like those of a Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Within to the Crown Prince were created early in the Jin, with duties comparable to those of a Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 食官令，一人。

translations.literal: Master of Victuals, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Victuals: one office.

sentences.zh: 職如太官令。

translations.literal: Duties like those of the Grand Master of Victuals.
translations.idiomatic: The duties were like those of the Grand Master of Victuals.

sentences.zh: 漢東京官也。

translations.literal: An office of the Eastern Han capital.
translations.idiomatic: This was an Eastern Han capital office.

sentences.zh: 今屬中庶子。

translations.literal: Now it belongs to the Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Today it reports to the Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 庶子，四人。

translations.literal: Attendants to the Crown Prince, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants to the Crown Prince: four offices.

sentences.zh: 職比散騎常侍、中書監令。

translations.literal: Duties comparable to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director and Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Their standing was comparable to that of a Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary or the Director and Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉制也。

translations.literal: This was a Jin regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This arrangement dated from the Jin.

sentences.zh: 漢西京員五人，漢東京無員，職如三署中郎。

translations.literal: The Western Han capital had a quota of five persons; the Eastern Han capital had no fixed quota; duties like those of the gentlemen-of-the-household in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: At the Western Han capital the quota was five; at the Eastern Han capital there was no fixed quota. Their duties were like those of the gentlemen-of-the-household in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 古者諸侯世祿，卿大夫之子即為副倅，謂之國子，天子諸侯子有庶子之官，以掌教之，秦因其名也。

translations.literal: In antiquity feudal lords held hereditary stipends; sons of ministers and grandees became deputy aides and were called sons of the state; sons of the Son of Heaven and feudal lords had the office of Attendant to the Heir to manage their instruction; Qin took its name from this.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity feudal lords held hereditary stipends, and the sons of ministers and grandees served as deputy aides called sons of the state; the sons of the Son of Heaven and of feudal lords had Attendants to the Heir to oversee their instruction, and the Qin borrowed the title.

sentences.zh: 秩四百石。

translations.literal: Rank of four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was four hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 舍人，十六人。

translations.literal: Attendants, sixteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants: sixteen offices.

sentences.zh: 職如散騎、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Duties like those of Cavalier Attendant and Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Their duties were like those of a Cavalier Attendant or Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉制也。

translations.literal: This was a Jin regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This arrangement dated from the Jin.

sentences.zh: 二漢無員，掌宿衛如三署中郎。

translations.literal: Neither Han dynasty had a fixed quota; they managed palace guard like the gentlemen-of-the-household in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Han dynasty set a fixed quota; they handled palace guard duty like the gentlemen-of-the-household in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 洗馬，八人。

translations.literal: Grooms-in-Waiting, eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms-in-Waiting: eight offices.

sentences.zh: 職如謁者、秘書郎也。

translations.literal: Duties like those of Herald and Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Their duties were like those of a Herald or Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 二漢員十六人。

translations.literal: Under both Han dynasties the quota was sixteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han dynasties the quota was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 太子出，則當直者前驅導威儀。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went out, those on duty rode ahead as vanguard to guide the ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went abroad, the officer on duty rode ahead as vanguard to lead the ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 秩比六百石。

translations.literal: Rank comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was comparable to six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 太子左衛率，七人。

translations.literal: Left Guard Commandant to the Crown Prince, seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Commandant to the Crown Prince: seven offices.

sentences.zh: 太子右衛率，二人。

translations.literal: Right Guard Commandant to the Crown Prince, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Commandant to the Crown Prince: two offices.

sentences.zh: 二率職如二衛。

translations.literal: The two commandants' duties were like those of the two guards.
translations.idiomatic: The two commandants had duties like those of the two guard generals.

sentences.zh: 秦時直雲衛率，漢因之。

translations.literal: In Qin times it was simply called Guard Commandant; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin the post was simply called Guard Commandant, and the Han kept the title.

sentences.zh: 主門衛。

translations.literal: They managed gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded gate security.

sentences.zh: 晉初曰中衛率，泰始分為左右，各領一軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin it was called Central Guard Commandant; in Taishi it was divided into left and right, each leading one army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin it was called Central Guard Commandant; in the Taishi era it was split into left and right, each commanding an army.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時，湣懷太子在東宮，加置前後二率。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Hui, when Crown Prince Minhuai was in the Eastern Palace, front and rear commandants were added.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's reign, while Crown Prince Minhuai occupied the Eastern Palace, front and rear commandants were added.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎為太弟，又置中衛，是為五率。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying became Grand Heir-apparent, a central guard was also established, making five commandants.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying was made Grand Heir-apparent, a central guard was added as well, for a total of five commandants.

sentences.zh: 江左初，省前後二率。

translations.literal: At the beginning after crossing south, the front and rear commandants were cut.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, the front and rear commandants were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元中又置。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era of Emperor Xiaowu they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, during the Taiyuan era, they were restored.

sentences.zh: 皆有丞，晉初置。

translations.literal: All had assistant directors, established at the beginning of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Each had an assistant director, a post created early in the Jin.

sentences.zh: 宋世止置左右二率。

translations.literal: In the Song era only the left and right commandants were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liu Song only the left and right commandants were retained.

sentences.zh: 秩舊四百石。

translations.literal: Formerly the rank was four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The former rank was four hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 太子屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavalry to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Commandant of Foot Soldiers to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Foot Soldiers to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Assisting Army to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Assisting Army to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三校尉各七人，並宋初置。

translations.literal: Each of the three commandants had seven persons; all were established at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three commandancies had seven officers; all were created at the founding of the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 屯騎、步兵，因台校尉；

translations.literal: Cavalry and Foot Soldiers followed the court commandants;
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry and Foot Soldiers posts followed the court commandancies;

sentences.zh: 翊軍，晉武帝太康初置，始為台校尉，而以唐彬居之，江左省。

translations.literal: Assisting Army was established at the beginning of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, first as a court commandant, with Tang Bin holding it; after crossing south it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The Assisting Army was created early in Emperor Wu's Taikang era as a court commandancy, first held by Tang Bin; after the move south it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太子冗從僕射，七人。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director to the Crown Prince, seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Attendant Vice Director to the Crown Prince: seven offices.

sentences.zh: 宋初置。

translations.literal: Established at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Created at the founding of the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 太子旅賁中郎將，十人。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Host Guard to the Crown Prince, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Host Guard to the Crown Prince: ten offices.

sentences.zh: 職如虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Duties like those of General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The duties were like those of the General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household of the Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 宋初置。

translations.literal: Established at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Created at the founding of the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 《周官》有旅賁氏。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had the Host Guard clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou already listed a Host Guard corps.

sentences.zh: 漢制，天子有虎賁，王侯有旅賁。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, the Son of Heaven had Tiger Guard; kings and marquises had Host Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han practice the emperor kept Tiger Guard, while kings and marquises kept Host Guard.

sentences.zh: 旅，眾也。

translations.literal: Host means multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Host means a host of men.

sentences.zh: 太子左積弩將軍，十人。

translations.literal: Left General of Accumulated Crossbows to the Crown Prince, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Left General of Accumulated Crossbows to the Crown Prince: ten offices.

sentences.zh: 太子右積弩將軍，二人。

translations.literal: Right General of Accumulated Crossbows to the Crown Prince, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Right General of Accumulated Crossbows to the Crown Prince: two offices.

sentences.zh: 漢東京積弩將軍，雜號也，無左右之積弩。

translations.literal: General of Accumulated Crossbows at the Eastern Han capital was a miscellaneous title; there were no left and right accumulated crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Han capital the General of Accumulated Crossbows was a miscellaneous title; there were no separate left and right accumulated-crossbow posts.

sentences.zh: 魏世至晉江左，左右積弩為台職，領營兵。

translations.literal: From the Wei through Jin east of the Yangzi, left and right accumulated crossbows were court offices leading camp troops.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei through the Jin, and after the move south, the left and right accumulated-crossbow generals were court posts commanding camp troops.

sentences.zh: 宋世度東宮，無複營矣。

translations.literal: In the Song era the posts passed to the Eastern Palace; there were no longer camps.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liu Song the posts were transferred to the Eastern Palace staff, and they no longer commanded camps.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍，十人。

translations.literal: Palace Hall General, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Hall General: ten offices.

sentences.zh: 殿中員外將軍，二十人。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Palace Hall General, twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Palace Hall General: twenty offices.

sentences.zh: 宋初置。

translations.literal: Established at the beginning of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Created at the founding of the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 平越中郎將，晉武帝置，治廣州，主南越。

translations.literal: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household Who Pacifies the Yue, established by Emperor Wu of Jin, administered Guang Province and managed the Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household Who Pacifies the Yue: created by Emperor Wu of Jin, with headquarters at Guang Province to oversee the Southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 南蠻校尉，晉武帝置，治襄陽。

translations.literal: Commandant Who Pacifies the Southern Man, established by Emperor Wu of Jin, administered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Who Pacifies the Southern Man: created by Emperor Wu of Jin, with headquarters at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 江左初省。

translations.literal: At the beginning after crossing south it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south it was initially abolished.

sentences.zh: 尋又置，治江陵。

translations.literal: Soon it was restored, administering Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon restored, with headquarters at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖孝建中省。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era of Emperor Shizu of Song it was cut.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished during Emperor Xiaowu's Xiaojian era.

sentences.zh: 西戎校尉，晉初置，治長安。

translations.literal: Commandant Who Pacifies the Western Rong, established at the beginning of Jin, administered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Who Pacifies the Western Rong: created early in the Jin, with headquarters at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙中又置，治漢中。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era of Emperor An it was restored, administering Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An, during the Yixi era, it was restored with headquarters at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 甯蠻校尉，晉武帝置，治襄陽，以授魯宗之。

translations.literal: Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, established by Emperor Wu of Jin, administered Xiangyang, and was granted to Lu Zongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Who Pacifies the Man: created by Emperor Wu of Jin, headquartered at Xiangyang, and granted to Lu Zongzhi.

sentences.zh: 南夷校尉，晉武帝置，治寧州。

translations.literal: Commandant Who Pacifies the Southern Yi, established by Emperor Wu of Jin, administered Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Who Pacifies the Southern Yi: created by Emperor Wu of Jin, with headquarters at Ning Province.

sentences.zh: 江左改曰鎮蠻校尉。

translations.literal: After crossing south the title was changed to Commandant Who Garrisons the Man.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south the title was changed to Commandant Who Garrisons the Man.

sentences.zh: 四夷中郎校尉，皆有長史、司馬、參軍。

translations.literal: The generals and commandants of the four barbarian directions all had chief clerks, masters of horse, and staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and commandants of the four frontier directions all had chief clerks, masters of horse, and staff officers.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉有雜號護軍，如將軍，今猶有鎮蠻、安遠等護軍。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin had miscellaneous Protectors of the Army, like generals; today there are still Protectors of the Army such as Who Garrisons the Man and Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei and Jin had miscellaneous Protectors of the Army, comparable to generals; today there are still such posts as Protector Who Garrisons the Man and Protector Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 鎮蠻以加廬江、晉熙、西陽太守。

translations.literal: Who Garrisons the Man was added to the Administrators of Lujiang, Jinxi, and Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Who Garrisons the Man was conferred on the Administrators of Lujiang, Jinxi, and Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 安遠以加武陵內史。

translations.literal: Who Pacifies the Distant was added to the Internal Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Who Pacifies the Distant was conferred on the Internal Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 刺史，每州各一人。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector, one person for each province.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector: one for each province.

sentences.zh: 黃帝立四監以治萬國，唐、虞世十二牧，是其職也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor established four overseers to govern the myriad states; in the ages of Tang and Yu there were twelve pastors—these were its duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor appointed four overseers to govern the myriad states, and under Tang and Yu there were twelve pastors—these were the antecedents of the office.

sentences.zh: 周改曰典，秦曰監禦史，而更遣丞相史分刺諸州，謂之刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou changed the title to overseer; Qin called them supervising censors, then further dispatched the chancellor's clerks to inspect the various provinces separately, calling them regional inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou renamed the post overseer; the Qin called them supervising censors, then sent the chancellor's clerks out to inspect the provinces in turn, whence the title Regional Inspector.

sentences.zh: 刺之為言，猶參覘也。

translations.literal: As for the word inspect, it is like to observe and watch.
translations.idiomatic: The word ci, to inspect, means to observe and scrutinize.

sentences.zh: 寫書亦謂之刺。

translations.literal: Copying documents is also called inspecting.
translations.idiomatic: Copying out documents was also called ci.

sentences.zh: 漢制，不得刺尚書事是也。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, that they may not inspect Secretariat affairs is this principle.
translations.idiomatic: This is the origin of the Han rule that regional inspectors may not interfere in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺史班行六條詔書，其一條曰，強宗豪右，田宅逾制，以強陵弱，以眾暴寡；

translations.literal: Regional inspectors circulated the six-article edict; the first article says: powerful clans and great families exceed regulations on fields and dwellings, using strength to bully the weak and numbers to overwhelm the few;
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspectors circulated a six-article edict. The first article read: powerful clans and great families exceed the limits on fields and dwellings, using strength to bully the weak and numbers to overwhelm the few;

sentences.zh: 其二條曰，二千石不奉詔書，遵承典制，背公向私，旁詔守利，侵漁百姓，聚斂為奸；

translations.literal: the second article says: two-thousand-bushel officials do not obey edicts or follow established regulations, turning from public to private, perverting edicts to hoard profit, encroaching on and exploiting the people, gathering wealth as wickedness;
translations.idiomatic: the second read: two-thousand-bushel officials fail to obey edicts or follow established regulations, turn from public duty to private gain, twist edicts to hoard profit, encroach on and exploit the people, and amass wealth through wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 其三條曰，二千石不恤疑獄，風厲殺人，怒則加罰，喜則任賞，煩擾苛暴，剝戮黎元，為百姓所疾，山崩石裂，妖詳訛言；

translations.literal: the third article says: two-thousand-bushel officials do not care for doubtful cases, kill in severe wind, add punishments in anger and give rewards at whim, harass with harsh cruelty, flay and slaughter the people, are hated by the commoners, and there are mountain collapses, stone splits, strange portents, and false rumors;
translations.idiomatic: the third read: two-thousand-bushel officials neglect doubtful cases, execute people in harsh severity, add punishments in anger and grant rewards on whim, harass the people with cruel oppression, flay and slaughter common folk until they are loathed by all—whereupon mountains collapse, stones split, and strange portents and false rumors arise;

sentences.zh: 其四條曰，二千石選署不平，苟阿所愛，蔽賢寵頑；

translations.literal: the fourth article says: two-thousand-bushel officials are unfair in selection and appointment, currying favor with those they love, hiding the worthy and pampering the stubborn;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth read: two-thousand-bushel officials are unfair in selection and appointment, currying favor with those they love, hiding the worthy and indulging the obstinate;

sentences.zh: 其五條曰，二千石子弟恃怙榮勢，請托所監；

translations.literal: the fifth article says: sons and younger brothers of two-thousand-bushel officials rely on glory and power, using connections within their jurisdiction;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth read: sons and younger brothers of two-thousand-bushel officials rely on family prestige and power, trading on connections within the inspector's jurisdiction;

sentences.zh: 其六條曰，二千石違公下比，阿附豪強，通行貨賂，割損正令。

translations.literal: the sixth article says: two-thousand-bushel officials violate public duty to band together below, cling to the powerful, traffic in bribes, and cut and damage proper laws.
translations.idiomatic: the sixth read: two-thousand-bushel officials abandon public duty to band together with subordinates, cling to the powerful, traffic in bribes, and undermine proper law.

sentences.zh: 歲終則乘傳詣京師奏事。

translations.literal: At year's end they rode relay horses to the capital to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they traveled by relay post to the capital to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 成帝綏和元年，改為牧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Suhe of Emperor Cheng, the title was changed to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Cheng's Suhe reign the title was changed to governor.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平二年，複為刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianping of Emperor Ai, it was restored as regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ai's Jianping reign it was restored to Regional Inspector.

sentences.zh: 前漢世，刺史乘傳周行郡國，無適所治。

translations.literal: In the Former Han era, regional inspectors rode relay horses touring commanderies and states in circuit, with no fixed place of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Han, regional inspectors traveled by relay post on circuit through the commanderies and kingdoms, with no fixed seat of administration.

sentences.zh: 後漢世，所治始有定處，止八月行部，不復奏事京師。

translations.literal: In the Later Han era, their place of administration first had a fixed location; they only toured departments in the eighth month and no longer reported affairs to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han they gained fixed seats of administration, toured their jurisdictions only in the eighth month, and no longer traveled to the capital to report.

sentences.zh: 晉江左猶行郡縣詔，棗據《追遠詩》曰：「先君為钜鹿太守，迄今三紀。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi under Jin they still circulated edicts through commanderies and counties; Zao Ju's "Poem Recalling the Distant" says: "My late father was Administrator of Julu; to this day three twelve-year cycles have passed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin crossed south, edicts were still circulated through the commanderies and counties. Zao Ju's "Poem Recalling the Distant" says: "My late father was Administrator of Julu; three twelve-year cycles have passed since then.

sentences.zh: 忝私為冀州刺史，班詔次於郡傳」是也。

translations.literal: I am privately honored as Regional Inspector of Jizhou, issuing the edict in turn at the commandery relay station"—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: I am privately honored as Regional Inspector of Jizhou, issuing the edict in turn at the commandery relay station." This is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 靈帝世，天下漸亂，豪桀各據有州郡，而劉焉、劉虞並自九卿出為益州、幽州牧，其任漸重矣。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Ling the realm gradually fell into disorder; powerful men each held provinces and commanderies, while Liu Yan and Liu Yu both came out from the Nine Ministers to become governors of Yizhou and Youzhou—their responsibilities gradually grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ling's reign the realm slid into disorder, and powerful men seized control of provinces and commanderies. Liu Yan and Liu Yu both left the Nine Ministers to become governors of Yizhou and Youzhou, and the office grew steadily weightier.

sentences.zh: 官屬有別駕從事史一人，從刺史行部；

translations.literal: Among the staff there was one Separate-Carriage Registrar, who accompanied the regional inspector on departmental tours;
translations.idiomatic: Among the staff was one Separate-Carriage Registrar, who accompanied the regional inspector on inspection tours;

sentences.zh: 治中從事史一人，主財穀簿書；

translations.literal: one Administrative Registrar, managing grain, revenue, and ledgers;
translations.idiomatic: one Administrative Registrar, in charge of grain, revenue, and account books;

sentences.zh: 兵曹從事史一人，主兵事；

translations.literal: one Military Affairs Registrar, managing military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: one Military Affairs Registrar, in charge of military affairs;

sentences.zh: 部從事史每郡各一人，主察非法；

translations.literal: one Department Registrar for each commandery, managing investigation of illegal acts;
translations.idiomatic: one Department Registrar for each commandery, charged with investigating illegal conduct;

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，錄閣下眾事，省署文書；

translations.literal: one chief recorder, recording all affairs below the pavilion and reviewing documents for issuance;
translations.idiomatic: one chief recorder, who recorded all business of the office and reviewed documents for issuance;

sentences.zh: 門亭長一人，主州正門；

translations.literal: one gate pavilion chief, managing the province's main gate;
translations.idiomatic: one gate pavilion chief, in charge of the provincial headquarters gate;

sentences.zh: 功曹書佐一人，主選用；

translations.literal: one merit officer recorder, managing selection and appointment;
translations.idiomatic: one merit officer recorder, in charge of selection and appointment;

sentences.zh: 《孝經》師一人，主試經；

translations.literal: one Classic of Filial Piety master, managing examination of the classics;
translations.idiomatic: one Classic of Filial Piety master, who tested candidates on the classics;

sentences.zh: 月令師一人，主時節祠祀；

translations.literal: one Monthly Ordinance master, managing seasonal rites and sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: one Monthly Ordinance master, in charge of seasonal rites and sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 律令師一人，平律；

translations.literal: one statutes and ordinances master, adjudicating law;
translations.idiomatic: one statutes and ordinances master, who adjudicated legal questions;

sentences.zh: 簿曹書佐一人，主簿書；

translations.literal: one ledger bureau recorder, managing account books;
translations.idiomatic: one ledger bureau recorder, in charge of account books;

sentences.zh: 典郡書佐每郡各一人，主一郡文書：漢制也。

translations.literal: one commandery documentation recorder for each commandery, managing one commandery's documents: this was Han regulation.
translations.idiomatic: one commandery documentation recorder for each commandery, in charge of that commandery's documents—this was Han practice.

sentences.zh: 今有別駕從事史、治中從事史、主簿、西曹書佐、祭酒從事史、議曹從事史、部郡從事史，自主簿以下，置人多少，各隨州，舊無定制也。

translations.literal: Today there are Separate-Carriage Registrar, Administrative Registrar, chief recorder, Western Bureau recorder, Libationer Registrar, Deliberation Bureau Registrar, and Commandery Department Registrar; from the chief recorder downward, how many persons are established varies with each province—formerly there was no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Today the staff includes a Separate-Carriage Registrar, an Administrative Registrar, a chief recorder, a Western Bureau recorder, a Libationer Registrar, a Deliberation Bureau Registrar, and Commandery Department Registrars. From the chief recorder down, the number of officers varies by province; there was never a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康中，江州又有別駕祭酒，居僚職之上，而別駕從事史如故，今則無也。

translations.literal: In the Xiankang era of Emperor Cheng of Jin, Jiang Province also had a Separate-Carriage Libationer, ranking above the other staff posts, while the Separate-Carriage Registrar remained as before; today this no longer exists.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Cheng's Xiankang era, Jiang Province also had a Separate-Carriage Libationer ranking above the other staff officers, while the Separate-Carriage Registrar remained unchanged; today that post no longer exists.

sentences.zh: 別駕、西曹主吏及選舉事，治中主眾曹文書事。

translations.literal: Separate-Carriage and Western Bureau managed clerks and selection and appointment affairs; Administrative managed the documentation affairs of all bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Separate-Carriage Registrar and Western Bureau handled clerical staff and selection and appointment; the Administrative Registrar handled documentation for all bureaus.

sentences.zh: 西曹，即漢之功曹書佐也。

translations.literal: Western Bureau is the Han merit officer recorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Bureau was the Han dynasty's merit officer recorder.

sentences.zh: 祭酒分掌諸曹兵、賊、倉、戶、水、鎧之屬。

translations.literal: The libationer divided management among the bureaus for military affairs, bandit suppression, granaries, households, waterworks, armor, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The libationer oversaw the bureaus for military affairs, bandit suppression, granaries, households, waterworks, armor, and the like.

sentences.zh: 揚州無祭酒，而主簿治事。

translations.literal: Yang Province had no libationer; the chief recorder managed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province had no libationer; the chief recorder handled business instead.

sentences.zh: 荊州有從事史，在議曹從事史下，大較應是魏、晉以來置也。

translations.literal: Jing Province had a registrar below the Deliberation Bureau registrar; broadly this should have been established from Wei and Jin onward.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province had an additional registrar ranking below the Deliberation Bureau registrar—likely a post created from the Wei and Jin dynasties onward.

sentences.zh: 今廣州、徐州有月令從事，若諸州之曹史，漢舊名也。

translations.literal: Today Guang Province and Xu Province have Monthly Ordinance registrars, like the bureau clerks of the various provinces—old Han names.
translations.idiomatic: Today Guang Province and Xu Province have Monthly Ordinance registrars, comparable to the bureau clerks of other provinces—survivals of old Han titles.

sentences.zh: 漢武元封四年，令諸州歲各舉秀才一人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Wu of Han, an order was issued that each province annually recommend one outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng reign (107 BCE), an edict ordered each province to recommend one outstanding talent every year.

sentences.zh: 後漢避光武諱，改茂才。

translations.literal: In Later Han, to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Guangwu, [the title] was changed to Maocai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han, to avoid the taboo on Emperor Guangwu's personal name, the title was changed to Maocai (Outstanding Talent).

sentences.zh: 魏復曰秀才。

translations.literal: Wei restored it as Xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the old name Xiucai (Outstanding Talent) was restored.

sentences.zh: 晉江左揚州歲舉二人，諸州舉一人，或三歲一人，隨州大小，並對策問。

translations.literal: Under Jin south of the Yangtze, Yang Province annually recommended two persons, the various provinces one each, or one every three years according to the province's size; all faced written examination questions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Jin, Yang Province recommended two candidates each year and the other provinces one apiece—or one every three years, depending on a province's size—and all were examined by written questions.

sentences.zh: 晉東海王越為豫州牧，牧置長史、參軍，庾凱為長史，謝鯤為參軍，此為牧者則無也。

translations.literal: Under Jin, when Prince of Donghai Sima Yue was Governor of Yu Province, the governorship established Chief Clerk and Military Aide; Yu Kai was Chief Clerk and Xie Kun Military Aide—where there was a governor, [the post of regional inspector] did not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, when Prince of Donghai Sima Yue served as Governor of Yu Province, the governor's office established a Chief Clerk and a Military Aide—Yu Kai as Chief Clerk and Xie Kun as Military Aide. Where a province had a governor, the regional inspector's post did not exist.

sentences.zh: 牧，二千石；

translations.literal: Governor, two thousand bushels;
translations.idiomatic: The governor ranked at two thousand bushels;

sentences.zh: 刺史，六百石。

translations.literal: regional inspector, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: the regional inspector at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 郡守，秦官。

translations.literal: Commandery Administrator, a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandery Administrator was a Qin dynasty office.

sentences.zh: 秦滅諸侯，隨以其地為郡，置守、丞、尉各一人。

translations.literal: Qin extinguished the feudal lords and immediately made their lands into commanderies, establishing one Administrator, one Assistant, and one Commandant in each.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin destroyed the feudal lords, it promptly converted their territories into commanderies, appointing one Administrator, one Assistant, and one Commandant in each.

sentences.zh: 守治民，丞佐之。

translations.literal: The Administrator governed the people; the Assistant assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator governed the people, and the Assistant supported him.

sentences.zh: 郡當邊戍者，丞為長史。

translations.literal: In commanderies stationed on the frontier, the Assistant served as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In frontier garrison commanderies, the Assistant served as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 晉江左皆謂之丞。

translations.literal: Under Jin south of the Yangtze all were called Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Jin, all were called Assistants.

sentences.zh: 尉典兵，備盜賊。

translations.literal: The Commandant managed troops and guarded against bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant commanded troops and guarded against bandits and thieves.

sentences.zh: 漢景帝中二年，更名守曰太守，尉為都尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Middle Period of Emperor Jing of Han, the Administrator was renamed Grand Administrator, and the Commandant became Commandant of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Jing's Middle Period reign, the Administrator was renamed Grand Administrator and the Commandant became Commandant of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 光武省都尉，後又往往置東部、西部都尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu eliminated the commandery commandant, but later Eastern and Western Commandants of the Commandery were often re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu abolished the commandery commandant, but Eastern and Western Commandants were often reinstated afterward.

sentences.zh: 有蠻夷者，又有屬國都尉。

translations.literal: Where there were barbarian tribes, there was also a Commandant of Dependent States.
translations.idiomatic: Where barbarian peoples lived, there was also a Commandant of Dependent States.

sentences.zh: 漢末及三國，多以諸部都尉為郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Han and in the Three Kingdoms period, departmental commandants were often used as commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Han and during the Three Kingdoms, departmental commandants were often converted into commanderies.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康七年，又省諸郡丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, commandery assistants were again eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Emperor Cheng's Xiankang reign, commandery assistants were abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖元嘉四年，復置。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Taizu of Song, they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Taizu's Yuanjia reign, they were restored.

sentences.zh: 郡官屬略如公府，無東西曹，有功曹史，主選舉，五官掾，主諸曹事，部縣有都郵、門亭長，又有主記史，催督期會，漢制也，今略如之。

translations.literal: Commandery staff posts broadly resembled those of a princely government; there was no Eastern or Western Bureau, but there was a Merit Officer Clerk managing selection and appointment, a Five-Offices Registrar managing the affairs of the various bureaus; among subordinate districts and counties there were District Postal Inspectors and Gate Pavilion Chiefs, and also Chief Recording Clerks who pressed for deadline assemblies—Han regulation, now broadly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery staff broadly resembled a princely household: there was no Eastern or Western Bureau, but a Merit Officer Clerk handled selection and appointment and a Five-Offices Registrar oversaw the bureaus. Subordinate districts and counties had District Postal Inspectors and Gate Pavilion Chiefs, and Chief Recording Clerks who enforced deadlines for assemblies—Han practice, still broadly followed today.

sentences.zh: 諸郡各有舊俗，諸曹名號，往往不同。

translations.literal: Each commandery had its own old customs; the titles of the various bureaus often differed.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandery kept its own old customs, and bureau titles often varied from place to place.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝納董仲舒之言，元光元年，始令郡國舉孝廉，制郡口二十萬以上，歲察一人；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han accepted Dong Zhongshu's advice; in the first year of Yuanguang, he first ordered commanderies and states to recommend Filially Pious and Incorrupt men, fixing that commanderies with populations above two hundred thousand should examine one person annually;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han took Dong Zhongshu's counsel, and in the first year of Yuanguang he first ordered commanderies and states to recommend Filially Pious and Incorrupt men, decreeing that commanderies with more than two hundred thousand registered persons should examine one candidate each year;

sentences.zh: 四十萬以上，二人；

translations.literal: above four hundred thousand, two persons;
translations.idiomatic: above four hundred thousand, two;

sentences.zh: 六十萬，三人；

translations.literal: six hundred thousand, three persons;
translations.idiomatic: six hundred thousand, three;

sentences.zh: 八十萬，四人；

translations.literal: eight hundred thousand, four persons;
translations.idiomatic: eight hundred thousand, four;

sentences.zh: 百萬，五人；

translations.literal: one million, five persons;
translations.idiomatic: one million, five;

sentences.zh: 百二十萬，六人；

translations.literal: one million two hundred thousand, six persons;
translations.idiomatic: one million two hundred thousand, six;

sentences.zh: 不滿二十萬，二歲一人；

translations.literal: below two hundred thousand, one person every two years;
translations.idiomatic: below two hundred thousand, one every two years;

sentences.zh: 不滿十萬，三歲一人。

translations.literal: below one hundred thousand, one person every three years.
translations.idiomatic: below one hundred thousand, one every three years.

sentences.zh: 限以四科，一曰德行高妙，志節清白；

translations.literal: They were limited to four categories: first, outstanding virtue and noble integrity of will and conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were confined to four categories: first, outstanding virtue and unsullied integrity of purpose;

sentences.zh: 二曰學通行修，經中博士；

translations.literal: second, thorough learning and cultivated conduct, fit to be Erudites of the classics;
translations.idiomatic: second, thorough learning and cultivated conduct, fit to serve as Erudites of the classics;

sentences.zh: 三曰明習法令，足以決疑，能案章覆問，文中禦史；

translations.literal: third, clear mastery of statutes and ordinances, sufficient to resolve doubts, able to review cases and re-examine them, fit for Palace Clerk or Censor;
translations.idiomatic: third, clear mastery of law, enough to resolve doubts, able to review cases and conduct follow-up inquiries, fit for Palace Clerk or Censor;

sentences.zh: 四曰剛毅多略，遭事不惑，明足決斷，材任三輔縣令。

translations.literal: fourth, resolute and resourceful, undaunted in crisis, clear-sighted enough to decide, talent suited for magistrates of the three metropolitan commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, resolute and resourceful, unshaken in emergencies, clear enough to decide, with talent suited to magistracies in the three metropolitan commanderies and their counties.

sentences.zh: 魏初，更制口十萬以上，歲一人，有秀異，不拘戶口。

translations.literal: In early Wei, the rule was revised: populations above one hundred thousand, one person annually; if outstanding talent appeared, household count was not binding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei the quota was revised to one candidate a year for populations above one hundred thousand; where exceptional talent appeared, household totals did not apply.

sentences.zh: 江左以丹陽、吳、會稽、吳興並大郡，歲各舉二人。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, Danyang, Wu, Kuaiji, and Wuxing were all large commanderies and each annually recommended two persons.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze, Danyang, Wu, Kuaiji, and Wuxing counted as large commanderies and each recommended two candidates every year.

sentences.zh: 漢制，歲遣上計掾史各一人，條上郡內眾事，謂之階簿，至今行之。

translations.literal: Under Han regulation, each year one Upper-Account Registrar and Clerk was dispatched, itemizing all affairs within the commandery, called the rank ledger—still practiced today.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han practice, each year one Upper-Account Registrar and Clerk was sent up to itemize all affairs within the commandery in what was called the rank ledger—a procedure still followed today.

sentences.zh: 太守，二千石；

translations.literal: Grand Administrator, two thousand bushels;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator ranked at two thousand bushels;

sentences.zh: 丞，六百石。

translations.literal: Assistant, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: the Assistant at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 縣令、長，秦官也。

translations.literal: County Magistrate and Chief, Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: The County Magistrate and County Chief were Qin dynasty offices.

sentences.zh: 大者為令，小者為長，侯國為相。

translations.literal: Large [counties] had Magistrates, small had Chiefs; marquisates had Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Large counties had Magistrates, smaller ones had Chiefs, and marquisates had Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 漢制，置丞一人，尉大縣二人，小縣一人。

translations.literal: Under Han regulation, one Assistant was established; large counties had two Commandants, small counties one.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han practice, each county had one Assistant; large counties had two Commandants and small counties one.

sentences.zh: 五家為伍，伍長主之；

translations.literal: Five households formed a squad; the squad chief presided over it;
translations.idiomatic: Five households formed a squad, headed by a squad chief;

sentences.zh: 二五為什，什長主之；

translations.literal: two squads formed a platoon; the platoon chief presided over it;
translations.idiomatic: two squads formed a platoon, headed by a platoon chief;

sentences.zh: 十什為裏，裏魁主之；

translations.literal: ten platoons formed a neighborhood; the neighborhood head presided over it;
translations.idiomatic: ten platoons formed a neighborhood, headed by a neighborhood chief;

sentences.zh: 十裏為亭，亭長主之；

translations.literal: ten neighborhoods formed a pavilion; the pavilion chief presided over it;
translations.idiomatic: ten neighborhoods formed a pavilion district, headed by a pavilion chief;

sentences.zh: 十亭為鄉，鄉有鄉佐、三老、有秩、嗇夫、遊徼各一人。

translations.literal: ten pavilions formed a township; the township had one Township Assistant, Three Elders, Paid Official, Requisition Chief, and Patrol Inspector each.
translations.idiomatic: ten pavilion districts formed a township, which had one Township Assistant, Three Elders, Paid Official, Requisition Chief, and Patrol Inspector.

sentences.zh: 鄉佐、有秩主賦稅，三老主教化，嗇夫主爭訟，遊徼主奸非。

translations.literal: The Township Assistant and Paid Official managed taxes and levies; the Three Elders managed moral education; the Requisition Chief managed litigation; the Patrol Inspector managed crime and wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: The Township Assistant and Paid Official handled taxes and levies, the Three Elders moral instruction, the Requisition Chief litigation, and the Patrol Inspector crime and misconduct.

sentences.zh: 其餘諸曹，略同郡職。

translations.literal: The remaining bureaus broadly matched commandery duties.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bureaus broadly corresponded to commandery offices.

sentences.zh: 以五官為廷掾，後則無複丞，唯建康有獄丞，其餘眾職，或此縣有而彼縣無，各有舊俗，無定制也。

translations.literal: The Five-Offices [chief] served as Court Registrar; later there was again no Assistant—only Jiankang had a Prison Assistant; the rest of the posts, some counties had and others lacked, each with old custom, no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Five-Offices chief served as Court Registrar. Later the Assistant was abolished again—only Jiankang kept a Prison Assistant. Other posts might exist in one county but not another, each place following old custom with no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 晉江右洛陽縣置六部都尉，餘大縣置二人，次縣、小縣各一人。

translations.literal: Under Jin west of the Yangtze, Luoyang County established six Department Commandants; remaining large counties two, intermediate and small counties one each.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Western Jin, Luoyang County had six Department Commandants; other large counties had two, and intermediate and small counties one each.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖元嘉十五年，縣小者又省之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Taizu of Song, small counties again eliminated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Emperor Taizu's Yuanjia reign, small counties abolished them once more.

sentences.zh: 諸官府至郡，各置五百者，舊說古君行師從，卿行旅從。

translations.literal: Every government office down to the commandery level each established a Five Hundred [officer]; old tradition says ancient rulers on campaign had army followers, high ministers on journey had brigade followers.
translations.idiomatic: Every government office down to the commandery level appointed a Five Hundred officer. Tradition held that ancient rulers on campaign traveled with an army retinue and high ministers with a brigade retinue.

sentences.zh: 旅，五百人也。

translations.literal: A brigade is five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: A brigade numbered five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 今縣令以上，古之諸侯，故立四五百以象師從旅從，依古義也。

translations.literal: Today's Magistrates and above correspond to ancient feudal lords, hence they establish four or five hundred [followers] to symbolize army and brigade retinues, following ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Today's magistrates and higher officials correspond to the feudal lords of old, so they appoint four or five hundred followers to symbolize army and brigade retinues, in keeping with ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 韋曜曰，五百字本為伍伯。

translations.literal: Wei Yao says the characters for Five Hundred originally stood for Squad-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao writes that the characters for "Five Hundred" originally meant Squad-Chief.

sentences.zh: 伍，當也；

translations.literal: Wu means "counter" or "match";
translations.idiomatic: Wu means "counter" or "match";

sentences.zh: 伯，道也。

translations.literal: bo means "path" or "way."
translations.idiomatic: bo means "path" or "way."

sentences.zh: 使之導引當道伯中以驅除也。

translations.literal: They were made to guide along the middle of the path and drive away [intruders].
translations.idiomatic: Their task was to guide the way along the middle of the road and drive off intruders.

sentences.zh: 周制，五百為旅，帥皆大夫，不得卑之如此說也。

translations.literal: Under Zhou regulation, five hundred formed a brigade, and their commanders were all grand masters—you cannot demean them as this explanation does.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou institutions, five hundred men formed a brigade and their commanders were grandees—so they cannot be reduced to an explanation like this.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》秋官有條狼氏，掌執鞭以趨辟，王出入則八人夾道，公則六人，侯伯則四人，子男則二人，近之矣，名之異爾。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Rites of Zhou the Autumn Office had the Wolf-Barrier Master, who wielded whips to hurry and clear the way; when the king went in and out, eight men flanked the road; a duke had six, marquises and earls four, viscounts and barons two—close to this, only the names differ.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also records a Wolf-Barrier Master in the Autumn Office who carried whips to hurry people aside and clear the road: when the king went out, eight men lined the way; a duke had six, marquises and earls four, viscounts and barons two. The practice is much the same; only the titles differ.

sentences.zh: 又《漢官》中有伯使，主為諸官驅使辟路于道伯中，故言伯使，此其比也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han Officials records a Chief Emissary, who drove officials to clear the path in the middle of the road—hence called Chief Emissary; this is comparable.
translations.idiomatic: Han Officials also mentions a Chief Emissary who drove officials to clear the middle of the road for them—hence the name Chief Emissary. This is a close parallel.

sentences.zh: 縣令，千石至六百石；

translations.literal: County Magistrate, from one thousand to six hundred bushels;
translations.idiomatic: The County Magistrate ranked from one thousand down to six hundred bushels;

sentences.zh: 長，五百石。

translations.literal: Chief, five hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: the County Chief at five hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 漢初，王國置太傅，掌輔導；

translations.literal: In early Han, kingdoms established a Grand Tutor, in charge of guidance and instruction;
translations.idiomatic: In early Han, each kingdom appointed a Grand Tutor to guide and instruct the prince;

sentences.zh: 內史主治民；

translations.literal: the Grand Administrator of the Interior governed the people;
translations.idiomatic: a Grand Administrator of the Interior governed the people;

sentences.zh: 丞相統眾官；

translations.literal: the Chancellor commanded all officials;
translations.idiomatic: a Chancellor commanded all officials;

sentences.zh: 中尉掌武職。

translations.literal: the Commandant of the Interior managed military duties.
translations.idiomatic: a Commandant of the Interior handled military affairs.

sentences.zh: 分官置職，略同京師。

translations.literal: Dividing offices and establishing posts broadly matched the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The division of offices broadly mirrored the capital.

sentences.zh: 至景帝懲七國之亂，更制諸王不得治國，漢為置吏，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官，其大夫、謁者、諸官長丞，皆損其員數。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing punished the Rebellion of the Seven States, he reformed so feudal princes could not govern their states; Han appointed officials for them, changed the title from chengxiang to xiang, eliminated Censor-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, Privy Treasurer, Director of the Imperial Clan, and Erudites; the Grand Masters, Ushers, and chiefs and assistants of the various offices—all had their quotas reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jing punished the Rebellion of the Seven States, he reformed the system so princes could no longer govern their own states. The Han court appointed officials for them, shortened the title from Chancellor-in-chief (chengxiang) to Chancellor (xiang), and abolished the Censor-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, Privy Treasurer, Director of the Imperial Clan, and Erudites. The quotas for Grandees, Ushers, and the chiefs and assistants of other offices were all cut back.

sentences.zh: 後改漢內史為京兆尹，中尉為執金吾，郎中令為光祿勳，而王國如故；

translations.literal: Later Han changed Grand Administrator of the Interior to Metropolitan Commandant, Commandant of the Interior to Bearer of the Mace, and Director of the Masters of Writing to Director of the Imperial Household, while kingdoms remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: Later the Han court renamed the Grand Administrator of the Interior Metropolitan Commandant, the Commandant of the Interior Bearer of the Mace, and the Director of the Masters of Writing Director of the Imperial Household, while kingdoms kept their old titles;

sentences.zh: 又太僕為僕，司農為大農。

translations.literal: also Grand Coachman became Coachman, and Minister of Revenue became Grand Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: and the Grand Coachman became Coachman and the Minister of Revenue Grand Revenues.

sentences.zh: 成帝更令相治民如郡太守，省內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng further ordered the Chancellor to govern the people like a commandery Grand Administrator, eliminating the Grand Administrator of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng further ordered the Chancellor to govern the people like a commandery Grand Administrator and abolished the Grand Administrator of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 其中尉如郡尉，太傅但曰傅。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Interior was like the Commandery Commandant; the Grand Tutor was simply called Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Interior corresponded to the Commandery Commandant, and the Grand Tutor was simply called Tutor.

sentences.zh: 漢東京亦置傅一人，王師事之；

translations.literal: The Eastern Han capital also established one Tutor, whom the prince served as teacher;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han capital also appointed one Tutor, whom the prince treated as his teacher;

sentences.zh: 相一人，主治民；

translations.literal: one Chancellor, mainly governing the people;
translations.idiomatic: one Chancellor, chiefly governing the people;

sentences.zh: 中尉一人，主盜賊；

translations.literal: one Commandant of the Interior, managing bandits and thieves;
translations.idiomatic: one Commandant of the Interior, in charge of bandits and thieves;

sentences.zh: 郎中令一人，掌郎中宿衛；

translations.literal: one Director of Palace Gentlemen, managing palace gentlemen and guard duty;
translations.idiomatic: one Director of Palace Gentlemen, commanding palace gentlemen on guard duty;

sentences.zh: 僕一人，治書一人，治書本曰尚書，後更名治書；

translations.literal: one Coachman, one Secretary—the Secretary was originally called Masters of Writing, later renamed Secretary;
translations.idiomatic: one Coachman and one Secretary—the Secretary was originally titled Masters of Writing and later renamed Secretary;

sentences.zh: 中大夫，無員，掌奉使京師及諸國；

translations.literal: Middle Grand Masters, without fixed quota, managing missions to the capital and to the various states;
translations.idiomatic: Middle Grandees, without fixed quota, handled missions to the capital and to other states;

sentences.zh: 謁者及禮樂、衛士、醫工、永巷、祀禮長各一人；

translations.literal: Ushers and chiefs of Music, Guards, Medical Officers, Long Corridors, and Sacrificial Ritual, one each;
translations.idiomatic: one each of Ushers and chiefs of Music, Guards, Medical Officers, Long Corridors, and Sacrificial Ritual;

sentences.zh: 郎中，無員。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Palace, without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the Palace, without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 魏氏謁者官屬，史闕不知次第。

translations.literal: Wei had Usher staff posts, but the records are missing and their sequence is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had Usher staff posts, but the records are lost and their order is unknown.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝初置師、友、文學各一人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wu of Jin, Teacher, Friend, and Literary Scholar were each established, one person each.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Wu of Jin's reign, Teacher, Friend, and Literary Scholar were each established, one to each post.

sentences.zh: 師即傅也，景帝諱師，改為傅。

translations.literal: Teacher is Grand Tutor; Emperor Jing tabooed shi, so it was changed to Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Teacher was the same office as Grand Tutor; Emperor Jing tabooed the character shi, so the title became Tutor.

sentences.zh: 宋世復改曰師。

translations.literal: Under Song it was again changed back to Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song dynasty the title was changed back to Teacher.

sentences.zh: 其文學，前漢已置也。

translations.literal: The Literary Scholar had already been established in Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Scholar had already existed in the Former Han.

sentences.zh: 友者，因文王、仲尼四友之名也。

translations.literal: Friend takes its name from King Wen and Confucius's Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Friend took its name from the Four Friends of King Wen and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 改太守為內史，省相及僕。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator was changed to Grand Administrator of the Interior; Chancellor and Coachman were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator was renamed Grand Administrator of the Interior, and the Chancellor and Coachman were abolished.

sentences.zh: 有郎中令、中尉、大農為三卿。

translations.literal: There were Director of Palace Gentlemen, Commandant of the Interior, and Grand Revenues as the three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Palace Gentlemen, Commandant of the Interior, and Grand Revenues formed the three chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 大國置左右常侍各三人，省郎中，置侍郎二人。

translations.literal: Large states established Left and Right Regular Attendants, three each; Gentlemen of the Palace were eliminated and Gentleman Attendants, two, were established.
translations.idiomatic: Large states appointed three Left and three Right Regular Attendants, abolished Gentlemen of the Palace, and established two Gentleman Attendants.

sentences.zh: 大國又置上軍、中軍、下軍三將軍；

translations.literal: Large states also established Upper Army, Middle Army, and Lower Army Generals;
translations.idiomatic: Large states also appointed Upper Army, Middle Army, and Lower Army Generals;

sentences.zh: 次國上軍將軍、下軍將軍各一人；

translations.literal: medium states one Upper Army General and one Lower Army General each;
translations.idiomatic: medium states one Upper Army General and one Lower Army General;

sentences.zh: 小國上軍而已。

translations.literal: small states only the Upper Army.
translations.idiomatic: small states only an Upper Army General.

sentences.zh: 典書、典祠、典衛、學官令、典書令丞各一人，治書四人，中尉、司馬、世子庶子陵廟、牧長各一人，謁者四人，中大夫六人，舍人十人，典醫丞、典府丞各一人。

translations.literal: Directors of Documentation, Sacrifice, and Guard, Literary Director, and Documentation Director Assistant one each; four Secretaries; one each of Commandant of the Interior, Master of Horse, Heir Apparent tutor, Secondary Son tutor, Mausoleum Director, and Pasture Chief; four Ushers; six Middle Grand Masters; ten Attendants; one each of Medical Director Assistant and Treasury Director Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There were one each of the Directors of Documentation, Sacrifice, and Guard, the Literary Director, and the Documentation Director's Assistant; four Secretaries; one each of Commandant of the Interior, Master of Horse, Heir Apparent tutor, Secondary Son tutor, Mausoleum Director, and Pasture Chief; four Ushers; six Middle Grandees; ten Attendants; and one each of Medical Director Assistant and Treasury Director Assistant.

sentences.zh: 宋氏以來，一用晉制，雖大小國，皆有三軍。

translations.literal: Since the Song clan, solely Jin regulation has been used; though large and small states differ, all have three armies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Liu Song dynasty, the Jin system has been used exclusively, and all states, large and small alike, have three armies.

sentences.zh: 晉制，典書令在常侍下，侍郎上；

translations.literal: Under Jin regulation, the Director of Documentation ranked below Regular Attendant and above Gentleman Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin system, the Director of Documentation ranked below Regular Attendant and above Gentleman Attendant;

sentences.zh: 江左則侍郎次常侍，而典書令居三軍下矣。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, Gentleman Attendant ranked next to Regular Attendant, and the Director of Documentation fell below the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze, Gentleman Attendant ranked immediately after Regular Attendant, and the Director of Documentation fell below the three army generals.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，公國則無中尉、常侍、三軍，侯國又無大農、侍郎，伯子男唯典書以下，又無學官令矣。

translations.literal: Since south of the Yangtze, duchies lacked Commandant of the Interior, Regular Attendant, and Three Armies; marquisates also lacked Grand Revenues and Gentleman Attendant; counts, viscounts, and barons had only Documentation Director and below, and also lacked Literary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Eastern Jin, duchies had no Commandant of the Interior, Regular Attendant, or Three Armies; marquisates also lacked Grand Revenues and Gentleman Attendant; counts, viscounts, and barons kept only the Documentation Director and lower posts, and even the Literary Director was omitted.

sentences.zh: 吏職皆以次損省焉。

translations.literal: Official posts were all reduced in succession accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Official posts were trimmed step by step in proportion to rank.

sentences.zh: 晉江右公侯以下置官屬，隨國小大，無定制也。

translations.literal: Under Jin west of the Yangtze, dukes and marquises and below established staff posts according to the state's size, with no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Western Jin, dukes, marquises, and lower nobles appointed staff according to the size of the fief, with no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 晉江左諸國，並三分食一。

translations.literal: Under Jin south of the Yangtze, all feudal states together received one-third [of fief revenue as stipend].
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Jin, all feudal states alike drew one-third of their fief's revenue as stipend.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興元年，始制九分食一

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan, the rule of one-ninth stipend was first established.
